_readme: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for tax-year figures. Pages reference keys via <Figure id="..."/>. Update here each fall when the IRS releases inflation adjustments; every page updates. Each entry: value, taxYear, source (Rev. Proc. / IRC / IRS page), verified (date).

abatement.6404f_window.value: the request must be submitted within the period allowed for collection of the penalty or addition to tax, or the penalty must have been paid within the period allowed for claiming a credit or refund of it
abatement.6404f_window.source: Instructions for Form 843 (rev. 12/2024), When to file — https://www.irs.gov/instructions/i843; IRC § 6404(f)

abatement.6676_penalty.value: 20% of the amount determined to be excessive, on an erroneous claim for refund or credit
abatement.6676_penalty.source: IRC § 6676(a), as described in the Instructions for Form 843 (rev. 12/2024) — https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/6676

abatement.843_claim_period.value: generally 3 years from the date the original return was filed or 2 years from the date the tax was paid, whichever is later
abatement.843_claim_period.source: Instructions for Form 843 (rev. 12/2024), Separate Form Required, page last reviewed 30 April 2026 — https://www.irs.gov/instructions/i843; IRC § 6511(a)

aca.ale_threshold.value: an employer who employed an average of at least 50 full-time employees on business days during the preceding calendar year

aca.aptc_repayment.value: repayable in full — the limitation in IRC § 36B(f)(2)(B) was removed for taxable years beginning after 31 December 2025
aca.aptc_repayment.source: Pub. L. 119-21 § 71305, as described in Rev. Proc. 2025-32 § 2.04 — https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/rp-25-32.pdf

aca.enhanced_percentages_expired.value: the temporary premium percentages likewise applied only to taxable years beginning after 31 December 2020 and before 1 January 2026

aca.ptc_cliff_restored.value: the suspension of the 400 percent ceiling applied only to taxable years beginning after 31 December 2020 and before 1 January 2026, so the ceiling operates again for 2026

aca.ptc_income_range.value: household income equal to or exceeding 100 percent but not exceeding 400 percent of the poverty line for the family size involved

aca.shared_responsibility.value: $0 — the applicable dollar amount under IRC § 5000A(c)(3)(A), with the percentage-of-income alternative at zero percent for taxable years beginning after 2015

adj.above_the_line_business.value: deductions attributable to a trade or business not consisting of the performance of services as an employee are taken in computing adjusted gross income — the gateway that makes several of these adjustments work

adj.alimony.value: no deduction — IRC § 215 was repealed by Pub. L. 115-97 § 11051(a), so payments under an instrument executed after 2018, or modified after that date to adopt the change, are neither deductible nor includible

adj.educator_expenses.value: $350 for 2026, for books, supplies other than nonathletic supplies for health or physical education courses, computer and other equipment, and supplementary materials used in the classroom — plus professional development courses

adj.eligible_educator.value: a kindergarten through grade 12 teacher, instructor, counselor, principal or aide in a school for at least 900 hours during a school year — so a college instructor is outside it

adj.moving_expenses.value: suspended for everyone except a member of the Armed Forces on active duty moving pursuant to a military order incident to a permanent change of station, and — from 2026 — an employee or new appointee of the intelligence community relocating on a change of assignment
adj.moving_expenses.source: IRC § 217(k)(1), (2), as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70113(a), (b) — https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/217

adj.reservist_travel.value: travel expenses at not more than the Federal per diem rates, incurred by a member of a reserve component performing services more than 100 miles from home

adj.student_loan_interest.value: interest paid during the year on any qualified education loan, capped at $2,500 — one cap per return, however many loans or students

adj.student_loan_phaseout.value: phased out for modified adjusted gross income above $85,000, or $175,000 on a joint return, and gone entirely at $100,000, or $205,000 on a joint return

adoption.credit.value: qualified adoption expenses up to $17,670, of which $5,120 is refundable, phasing out between $265,080 and $305,080 of modified adjusted gross income
adoption.credit.source: Rev. Proc. 2025-32 § 3.04(1)-(3); IRC § 23(a)(4) as added by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70402(a) — https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/rp-25-32.pdf

advice.client_information.value: a practitioner generally may rely in good faith without verification on information furnished by the client — but may not ignore the implications of information furnished to or actually known by them, and must make reasonable inquiries if the information appears incorrect, inconsistent with an important fact or another factual assumption, or incomplete

advice.penalty_warning.value: a practitioner must inform the client of any penalties reasonably likely to apply to a position on a return where the practitioner advised on it or prepared or signed the return, and to any document, affidavit or other paper submitted to the IRS — and must inform the client of any opportunity to avoid them by disclosure and of the requirements for adequate disclosure, whether or not the practitioner is themselves exposed

advice.reliance_on_others.value: a practitioner may rely on another person's advice only if it was reasonable and the reliance is in good faith on all the facts and circumstances — and reliance is not reasonable where the practitioner knows or reasonably should know that the opinion should not be relied on, that the person is not competent or lacks the necessary qualifications, or that the person has a conflict of interest in violation of Circular 230

advice.unreasonable_reliance.value: reliance on representations, statements, findings or agreements is unreasonable if the practitioner knows or reasonably should know that one or more of the representations, or assumptions on which any representation is based, are incorrect, incomplete or inconsistent

advice.written_requirements.value: 6 — base the advice on reasonable factual and legal assumptions including as to future events; reasonably consider all relevant facts and circumstances the practitioner knows or reasonably should know; use reasonable efforts to identify and ascertain the facts relevant to each Federal tax matter; not rely on representations, statements, findings or agreements of the taxpayer or anyone else where reliance would be unreasonable; relate applicable law and authorities to facts; and not take into account the possibility that a return will not be audited or a matter not raised on audit

alimony.repeal_date.value: divorce or separation instruments executed after 31 December 2018, and instruments executed on or before that date and modified afterwards where the modification expressly so provides
alimony.repeal_date.source: IRC § 215, repealed by Pub. L. 115-97 § 11051(a); effective date at § 11051(c)

amended.assessment_tail.value: where a signed document showing additional tax is received in the 60 days ending on the assessment deadline, the period for that additional amount runs 60 days from receipt

aotc.amount.value: $2,500 per eligible student — 100 percent of the first $2,000 of qualified tuition and related expenses plus 25 percent of the next $2,000 — of which 40 percent is refundable

appeals.ased_remaining.value: generally 365 days must remain on the assessment statute expiration date when Appeals receives the case, and at least 270 days on the non-extendable ASED for estate tax cases
appeals.ased_remaining.source: IRS Pub. 3498 (Rev. 5-2025), "Consents to Extend the Assessment Statute Expiration Date" — https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p3498.pdf

appeals.case_file_access.value: not later than 10 days before the date of the conference
appeals.case_file_access.source: IRC § 7803(e)(7), added by the Taxpayer First Act of 2019, read at law.cornell.edu

appeals.formal_protest_threshold.value: more than $25,000 of proposed change to total tax and penalties for any tax period
appeals.formal_protest_threshold.source: Publication 5, Your Appeal Rights and How to Prepare a Protest if You Disagree (Rev. 4-2021)

appeals.protest_contents.value: a statement that you want to appeal, plus name, address and daytime telephone number; a list of all disputed issues, tax periods, proposed changes and reasons for disagreement; the facts supporting your position on each issue; the law or authority, if any, supporting it; a penalties of perjury statement; and your or your representative's signature under it

appeals.protest_threshold.value: $25,000 or less in proposed change to tax and penalties (or claimed refund) for each tax period permits a small case request; more than $25,000 for any tax period requires a formal written protest
appeals.protest_threshold.source: IRS Pub. 5 (Rev. 4-2021), "Small Case Request" and "Formal Written Protest"; IRS Pub. 3498 (Rev. 5-2025), "The Examination Process" — https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p5.pdf

appeals.protest_window.value: the time limit specified in the letter — generally 30 days from the date of the letter
appeals.protest_window.source: IRS, "Preparing a request for appeals," page last reviewed 28 June 2026; IRS Pub. 3498 (Rev. 5-2025) — https://www.irs.gov/appeals/preparing-a-request-for-appeals

appeals.small_case_threshold.value: $25,000 or less of total tax and penalties for each tax period involved
appeals.small_case_threshold.source: Publication 5, Your Appeal Rights and How to Prepare a Protest if You Disagree (Rev. 4-2021)

appeals.specified_taxpayer.entity.value: gross receipts not exceeding $5 million for the taxable year to which the dispute relates
appeals.specified_taxpayer.entity.source: IRC § 7803(e)(7), added by the Taxpayer First Act of 2019, read at law.cornell.edu

appeals.specified_taxpayer.individual.value: adjusted gross income not exceeding $400,000 for the taxable year to which the dispute relates
appeals.specified_taxpayer.individual.source: IRC § 7803(e)(7), added by the Taxpayer First Act of 2019, read at law.cornell.edu

atin.deactivation.value: two years from issue, with a reminder notice sent at eighteen months
atin.deactivation.source: IRS, Adoption taxpayer identification number Q&A (page last reviewed 22 February 2026) — https://www.irs.gov/individuals/adoption-taxpayer-identification-number

atin.qualifications.value: 5 — the child is legally placed in the home for legal adoption by an authorized placement agency; the adoption is domestic, or foreign with a Permanent Resident Alien Card or Certificate of Citizenship; the child's existing SSN cannot be obtained despite reasonable attempts; an SSN cannot be obtained from the SSA; and the taxpayer is eligible to claim the child as a dependent
atin.qualifications.source: IRS, Adoption taxpayer identification number Q&A, A4 (page last reviewed 22 February 2026)

auditrecon.collection_response.value: collection may be delayed on receipt, but may resume if the documentation does not support the position and the taxpayer does not answer a request for more information within 30 calendar days

auditrecon.criteria.value: a return was filed; the assessment is unpaid or credits were reversed; the disputed adjustments are identified; and either new information not previously considered is supplied, or the IRS made a computational or processing error

authority.ceases.value: an authority stops being one to the extent it is overruled or modified, implicitly or explicitly, by a body with power to do so — but a Tax Court opinion is not treated as overruled by a court of appeals to which the taxpayer has no right of appeal unless the Tax Court adopts that holding, and a private letter ruling is not authority if revoked or inconsistent with a later proposed regulation, revenue ruling or IRB pronouncement

authority.list.value: applicable provisions of the Code and other statutes; proposed, temporary and final regulations construing them; revenue rulings and revenue procedures; tax treaties and regulations thereunder and official explanations of them; court cases; congressional intent in committee reports, conference-report joint explanatory statements and pre-enactment floor statements by a bill's managers; Joint Committee on Taxation General Explanations (the Blue Book); private letter rulings and technical advice memoranda issued after 31 October 1976; actions on decisions and general counsel memoranda issued after 12 March 1981, and GCMs in pre-1955 Cumulative Bulletin volumes; IRS information or press releases; and notices, announcements and other administrative pronouncements published in the Internal Revenue Bulletin

authority.not_authority.value: conclusions reached in treatises, legal periodicals, legal opinions, or opinions rendered by tax professionals — though the authorities underlying those opinions may themselves give rise to substantial authority

authority.substantial_standard.value: an objective standard, less stringent than more likely than not (a greater than 50-percent likelihood) but more stringent than reasonable basis; met only where the weight of supporting authorities is substantial in relation to the weight of contrary authorities, all relevant authorities being taken into account

authority.written_determination.value: a ruling, determination letter, technical advice memorandum, or Chief Counsel advice; unless the Secretary provides otherwise by regulation it may not be used or cited as precedent — yet it does give the taxpayer it was issued to substantial authority for that treatment

awards.employee_achievement.value: $400 for an award that is not a qualified plan award, and $1,600 counting all such awards to the employee for the year including non-qualified ones — neither figure indexed

backup.withholding_rate.value: the fourth lowest rate applicable under IRC § 1(c), which is 24 percent for 2026
backup.withholding_rate.source: IRC § 3406(a)(1); IRC § 1(c) as adjusted by Rev. Proc. 2025-32 § 3.01 — https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/3406

baddebt.amount.value: the adjusted basis provided in IRC § 1011 for determining loss on a sale — so a cash-method lender's unpaid interest, never included in income, has no basis and produces no deduction

baddebt.bona_fide.value: only a bona fide debt qualifies — one arising from a debtor-creditor relationship based on a valid and enforceable obligation to pay a fixed or determinable sum; a gift or a contribution to capital is not a debt

baddebt.debtor_use_irrelevant.value: the use the debtor puts the borrowed funds to is of no consequence — the character is fixed by the creditor's relation to the loss

baddebt.nonbusiness_character.value: the general bad debt deduction does not apply; a nonbusiness debt becoming worthless is a loss from the sale or exchange of a capital asset held **not more than 1 year** — short-term capital loss, whatever the age of the debt

baddebt.nonbusiness_definition.value: any debt other than one created or acquired in connection with the taxpayer's trade or business, or one whose worthlessness is incurred in that trade or business — a question of fact, turning on whether the loss bears a proximate relation to a business the taxpayer carries on when the debt goes bad

baddebt.refund_period.value: seven years from the date the return was required to be filed, in place of the ordinary period, for a refund claim relating to the deductibility of a worthless debt or security or its effect on a carryover

baddebt.wholly_worthless_only.value: no partial deduction — a loss on a nonbusiness debt is treated as sustained only if and when the debt has become totally worthless

baddebt.worthless_security.value: a security that is a capital asset and becomes worthless is a loss from a sale on the **last day of the taxable year**, which can turn a short holding into a long-term loss; such a debt is outside the nonbusiness bad debt rules

basis.adjustments.value: reduced for depreciation, amortisation and depletion to the extent allowed and producing a tax reduction, but **not less than the amount allowable** — and where no method was adopted, the allowable amount is computed straight line
basis.adjustments.source: IRC § 1016(a)(2)(A), (B) and its closing flush text — https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/1016

basis.community_property.value: the surviving spouse's own one-half share of community property takes a new basis too, where at least one-half of the whole community interest was includible in the decedent's gross estate — so the entire asset is stepped, not half of it

basis.cost.value: the cost of the property, except as subchapters O, C, K and P provide otherwise — and cost excludes any amount for real property taxes treated under IRC § 164(d) as imposed on the taxpayer

basis.deathbed_gift.value: no step-up — where appreciated property was given to the decedent within the 1-year period ending on the date of death and passes back to the donor or the donor's spouse, basis is the decedent's adjusted basis immediately before death

basis.gift.value: the donor's basis carries over, except that where that basis exceeds the property's fair market value at the time of the gift, the fair market value is used **for determining loss** — so a gift of depreciated property has two bases and can produce neither gain nor loss

basis.gift_tax_adjustment.value: increased by the gift tax paid, but not above fair market value at the time of the gift — and for gifts after 31 December 1976 only by the fraction of that tax which the net appreciation bears to the amount of the gift

basis.holding_period_tacking.value: the prior holder's period is included wherever the property takes that person's basis in whole or in part for determining gain or loss — and property acquired from a decedent whose basis is determined under IRC § 1014 is treated as held more than one year however soon it is sold

basis.inherited.value: fair market value at the date of the decedent's death, or its value at the applicable valuation date where an IRC § 2032 election is made, or its § 2032A value, or the decedent's basis to the extent of the § 2031(c) exclusion

basis.inherited_consistency.value: capped at the final value determined for estate tax purposes, or the value in a statement furnished under IRC § 6035(a) — but only where including the property increased the estate's chapter 11 liability net of credits

basis.spousal_transfer.value: no gain or loss on a transfer to a spouse, or to a former spouse incident to divorce; the property is treated as acquired by gift and the transferee takes the transferor's adjusted basis — with no fair market value limitation for loss

basis.unknown_donor_basis.value: the Secretary is directed to obtain the facts from the donor or a person cognizant of them; only where that proves impossible is fair market value at the donor's acquisition substituted

belowmarket.de_minimis.value: $10,000 of aggregate outstanding gift loans between individuals, and the same figure for compensation-related and corporate-shareholder loans, neither exception applying where a principal purpose is tax avoidance

belowmarket.net_investment_cap.value: for gift loans between individuals not exceeding $100,000, the amount treated as retransferred to the lender cannot exceed the borrower's net investment income for the year

burden.7491_conditions.value: 3 — the taxpayer has complied with the substantiation requirements of the Code; has maintained all required records and cooperated with reasonable requests for witnesses, information, documents, meetings and interviews; and, for a partnership, corporation or trust, meets the net worth and employee limits of IRC § 7430(c)(4)(A)(ii)

burden.7491_entity_limits.value: net worth not exceeding $7,000,000 and not more than 500 employees at the time the action was filed (individuals: net worth not exceeding $2,000,000)

burden.default.value: on the petitioner, except as otherwise provided by statute or determined by the Court — and on the respondent as to any new matter, increases in deficiency, and affirmative defenses pleaded in the answer

burden.fraud.value: on the respondent, carried by clear and convincing evidence

burden.penalties.value: the Secretary carries the burden of production in any court proceeding as to the liability of any individual for any penalty, addition to tax, or additional amount

caf.future_horizon.value: future tax periods may not exceed 3 years from 31 December of the year the IRS receives the power of attorney; periods beyond that are not recorded but the authorization stays valid and may be resubmitted
caf.future_horizon.source: Instructions for Form 2848 (rev. 09/2021), line 3, page last reviewed 30 April 2026 — https://www.irs.gov/instructions/i2848. Compare 26 CFR § 601.506(d)(3)(ii), which measures 3 years from the date of receipt.

caf.representative_limit.value: 3 representatives under a power of attorney, or 3 persons under a tax information authorization; where more are named only the first 3 are recorded, though all remain appointed

capgain.adjusted_net_capital_gain.value: net capital gain reduced by unrecaptured section 1250 gain and by 28-percent rate gain, plus qualified dividend income — the residue is what the 0, 15 and 20 percent rates reach

capgain.capital_asset.value: all property held by the taxpayer, business or not, except eight listed classes — inventory and property held for sale to customers, depreciable and real property used in the trade or business, self-created intangibles, trade receivables, government publications, certain commodities derivatives, hedging transactions, and supplies

capgain.carryover.value: the excess is carried to the succeeding year, short-term and long-term separately, each retaining its character, with no expiry

capgain.collectibles.value: 28 percent — collectibles gain and section 1202 gain, net of collectibles loss, the net short-term capital loss and long-term capital loss carried forward, where a collectible takes its IRC § 408(m) meaning without regard to paragraph (3)

capgain.digital_assets.value: property, not currency — general property principles apply and no foreign currency gain or loss arises; a digital asset is separately defined for broker reporting as a digital representation of value recorded on a cryptographically secured distributed ledger

capgain.fifteen_rate_amount.value: $613,700 joint or surviving spouse; $579,600 head of household; $545,500 single; $306,850 married filing separately; $16,250 estates and trusts

capgain.holding_period.value: more than 1 year for long term, not more than 1 year for short term — so property bought on a given date first qualifies when sold on the day after the anniversary

capgain.loss_limit.value: capital losses are allowed against capital gains in full, plus the lower of $3,000 — $1,500 for a married individual filing a separate return — or the excess of losses over gains; unindexed since 1986 and not doubled on a joint return

capgain.mark_to_market_1256.value: each section 1256 contract held at year end is treated as sold at fair market value on the last business day, and gain or loss is 40 percent short-term and 60 percent long-term whatever the actual holding period

capgain.mutual_fund_distributions.value: a capital gain dividend is treated by the shareholder as gain from the sale of a capital asset held more than one year, whatever the shareholder's own holding period in the fund

capgain.niit.value: 3.8 percent of the lesser of net investment income or the excess of modified adjusted gross income over the threshold — $250,000 joint or surviving spouse, half that for married filing separately, $200,000 otherwise, none of them indexed

capgain.qualified_dividend_holding.value: the stock must be held more than 60 days during the 121-day period around the ex-dividend date; for preference dividends attributable to periods aggregating more than 366 days, more than 90 days during a 181-day period
capgain.qualified_dividend_holding.source: IRC § 1(h)(11)(B)(iii)(I), applying IRC § 246(c)(1)(A), (c)(2) with the substituted figures — https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/1

capgain.rate_structure.value: 0 percent up to the maximum zero rate amount, 15 percent up to the maximum 15-percent rate amount, and 20 percent above it — with the § 1(h)(1)(B) and (C)(ii)(I) references to a rate below 25 percent and below 39.6 percent replaced by those defined amounts

capgain.self_created.value: excluded from capital asset treatment in the creator's hands — a patent, invention, model or design, secret formula or process, copyright, or literary, musical or artistic composition; but the taxpayer may elect capital treatment for musical compositions and copyrights in musical works

capgain.wash_sale.value: no deduction where substantially identical stock or securities are acquired within 30 days before or after the sale, and the disallowed loss is added to the basis of the replacement — the section reaches stock or securities, and contracts or options to acquire or sell them

capgain.zero_rate_amount.value: $98,900 joint or surviving spouse; $66,200 head of household; $49,450 single or married filing separately; $3,300 estates and trusts

carryover.amt_credit.value: the adjusted net minimum tax imposed for all prior taxable years beginning after 1986, less amounts already allowed as a credit

carryover.capital_loss_annual.value: $3,000, or $1,500 for a married individual filing a separate return

carryover.capital_loss_period.value: indefinite, with the short-term and long-term components carried forward separately and retaining their character

carryover.charitable_period.value: the 5 succeeding taxable years, in order of time, subject in each year to the same percentage limitation

carryover.nol_limit.value: the deduction for post-2017 losses is capped at 80 percent of taxable income computed without the § 172, § 199A and § 250 deductions, while pre-2018 losses are deductible in full and are taken first (IRC § 172(a)(2))

carryover.nol_period.value: a net operating loss arising in a taxable year beginning after 31 December 2017 carries forward to each taxable year following the loss, with no expiry and — outside the farming and insurance exceptions — no carryback (IRC § 172(b)(1)(A)(ii)(II))

carryover.passive.value: indefinite — a loss or credit disallowed under IRC § 469(a) is treated as allocable to the same activity in the next taxable year, and is released on a fully taxable disposition of the entire interest (IRC § 469(b), (g))

caselaw.acquiescence.value: 3 recommendations — acquiescence, meaning the IRS accepts the holding and will follow it on the same controlling facts, indicating neither approval nor disapproval of the court's reasons; acquiescence in result only, same acceptance but signalling disagreement or concern with some or all of those reasons; and nonacquiescence, meaning the IRS does not agree and generally will not follow the decision for other taxpayers, though it recognises the precedential impact within the deciding circuit

caselaw.aod.value: issued at the IRS's discretion only on unappealed issues decided adverse to the government; it is not an affirmative statement of IRS position, is not intended as public guidance, and may not be cited as precedent — relied on within the IRS only as the conclusion applying the law to the facts of that case at that time

caselaw.taxcourt_opinions.value: 3 — regular opinions, which involve more than mere factual determinations or applications of well-established principles and generally decide new points of law that set precedents; memorandum decisions, which primarily involve factual determinations and the application of well-established rules; and small tax case decisions, which are final, may not be appealed by either party, and have no precedential value

caselaw.weight.value: a Supreme Court decision becomes the law of the land, takes precedence over lower courts, must be followed by the IRS, and for examiners has the same weight as the Code; decisions of the Tax Court, District Courts and the Court of Federal Claims bind the IRS only for the particular taxpayer and the years litigated, and an adverse lower-court decision does not require the IRS to alter its position for other taxpayers

casualty.above_the_line_portion.value: personal casualty losses up to the amount of personal casualty gains are allowable in computing adjusted gross income rather than as an itemized deduction

casualty.agi_floor.value: where personal casualty losses exceed personal casualty gains, the losses are allowed only to the extent of the gains plus so much of the excess as exceeds 10 percent of adjusted gross income

casualty.disaster_requirement.value: a personal casualty loss is deductible only to the extent attributable to a **Federally declared disaster or a State declared disaster** — the State limb added by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70109(b)(1), and the restriction made permanent by the same section
casualty.disaster_requirement.source: IRC § 165(h)(5)(A), as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70109(a), (b)(1) — https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/165

casualty.gains_exceed_losses.value: where personal casualty gains exceed personal casualty losses, all the gains and all the losses are treated as from sales or exchanges of capital assets — so the 10 percent floor never applies

casualty.gains_exception.value: where there are personal casualty gains, the disaster requirement does not apply to non-disaster losses up to the amount of those gains — and the gains so used are then removed from the § 165(h)(2)(A) computation for the disaster losses

casualty.per_event_floor.value: $100 per casualty or per theft for taxable years beginning after 31 December 2009 — applied to each event separately before anything else

casualty.prior_year_election.value: a loss occurring in a disaster area and attributable to a federally declared disaster may, at the taxpayer's election, be taken into account for the taxable year immediately preceding the year in which the disaster occurred

casualty.state_declared.value: any natural catastrophe — hurricane, tornado, storm, high water, wind-driven water, tidal wave, tsunami, earthquake, volcanic eruption, landslide, mudslide, snowstorm or drought — or, regardless of cause, any fire, flood or explosion, which the Governor and the Secretary determine causes damage of sufficient severity and magnitude
casualty.state_declared.source: IRC § 165(h)(5)(C)(i), as added by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70109(b) — https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/165

cdp.equivalent_hearing_window.value: one year — for a lien, commencing the day after the end of the five-business-day period following the NFTL filing; for a levy, commencing the day after the date of the CDP notice

cdp.response_days.value: 30 days — for a lien, beginning the day after the 5-business-day period following the NFTL filing; for a levy, the 30-day period after the final notice

cfs.effective_date.source: IRS Collection Financial Standards, effective June 29, 2026 (irs.gov national/local standards pages)

cfs.health.65_and_over.source: IRS Collection Financial Standards, effective June 29, 2026 (irs.gov national/local standards pages)

cfs.health.under_65.source: IRS Collection Financial Standards, effective June 29, 2026 (irs.gov national/local standards pages)

cfs.housing_document_pages.source: IRS Collection Financial Standards, effective June 29, 2026 (irs.gov national/local standards pages)

cfs.national.additional_person.value: $397 per month for each person beyond four
cfs.national.additional_person.source: IRS Collection Financial Standards, effective June 29, 2026 (irs.gov national/local standards pages)

cfs.national.four_persons.source: IRS Collection Financial Standards, effective June 29, 2026 (irs.gov national/local standards pages)

cfs.national.one_person.source: IRS Collection Financial Standards, effective June 29, 2026 (irs.gov national/local standards pages)

cfs.national.three_persons.source: IRS Collection Financial Standards, effective June 29, 2026 (irs.gov national/local standards pages)

cfs.national.two_persons.source: IRS Collection Financial Standards, effective June 29, 2026 (irs.gov national/local standards pages)

cfs.transport.ownership_one_car.source: IRS Collection Financial Standards, effective June 29, 2026 (irs.gov national/local standards pages)

cfs.transport.ownership_two_cars.source: IRS Collection Financial Standards, effective June 29, 2026 (irs.gov national/local standards pages)

cfs.transport.public.source: IRS Collection Financial Standards, effective June 29, 2026 (irs.gov national/local standards pages)

charity.appraisal_thresholds.value: a deduction of more than $500 for contributed property requires the § 170(f)(11) documentation; more than $5,000 requires a qualified appraisal to be obtained; more than $500,000 requires the appraisal itself to be attached to the return

charity.cash_limit.value: 60 percent of the contribution base for cash contributions to a § 170(b)(1)(A) organization, reduced by the contributions already taken into account under that subparagraph — and now permanent, the 2026 end date having been struck
charity.cash_limit.source: IRC § 170(b)(1)(G)(i)(I), (II), as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70425(b)(1) — https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/170

charity.contribution_base.value: adjusted gross income, computed without regard to any net operating loss carryback to the year under IRC § 172

charity.cwa_contemporaneous.value: obtained on or before the earlier of the date the return for the year of the contribution is filed, or the due date including extensions for that return

charity.cwa_contents.value: 3 items — the amount of cash and a description (but not value) of any non-cash property contributed; whether the donee provided any goods or services in consideration; and a description and good faith estimate of the value of any such goods or services, or a statement that they consisted solely of intangible religious benefits

charity.cwa_threshold.value: $250 or more per contribution, requiring a contemporaneous written acknowledgment from the donee organization

charity.floor.value: 0.5 percent of the contribution base — any otherwise allowable charitable contribution is allowed only to the extent the aggregate exceeds it, and the floor is absorbed against the categories in a prescribed order ending with the 60 percent cash category
charity.floor.source: IRC § 170(b)(1)(I), as added by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70425(a)(1) — https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/170

charity.non_itemizer.value: a deduction of up to $1,000, or $2,000 on a joint return, for cash contributions to a § 170(b)(1)(A) organization — but not to a § 509(a)(3) supporting organization and not to establish or maintain a donor advised fund

charity.readily_valued_exception.value: the appraisal requirements do not apply to cash, inventory, publicly traded securities, or a qualified vehicle for which the donee acknowledgement is provided

charity.recordkeeping.value: no deduction for **any** cash, check or other monetary gift, of any amount, without a bank record or written communication from the donee showing its name, the date and the amount

charity.substantiation_250.value: no deduction for a contribution of $250 or more without a contemporaneous written acknowledgment from the donee stating the amount of cash and a description of any property, whether goods or services were provided in consideration, and a good faith estimate of their value

circ230.10_51.categories.value: 18 enumerated categories, expressly a non-exhaustive list

circ230.agency_decision.days.value: 180 days after receipt of the appeal

circ230.alj.decision_days.value: 180 days after the hearing closes and proposed findings are received

circ230.answer.min_days.value: not less than 30 days from service of the complaint

circ230.appeal.days.value: 30 days from service of the Administrative Law Judge decision

circ230.expedited.lookback.value: conduct within the 5 years before the show cause order is served

circ230.expedited.nonfiling.value: no annual return in 4 of the 5 preceding tax years, or no more-frequent return in 5 of the 7 preceding tax periods, and still noncompliant when the suspension notice issues

circ230.monetary_penalty.cap.value: not more than the gross income derived, or to be derived, from the conduct giving rise to the penalty

circ230.reinstatement.period.value: 5 years after disbarment, suspension or disqualification, or immediately after a shorter period expires

circ230.standard_of_proof.value: preponderance of the evidence for censure or suspension under six months; clear and convincing evidence for a monetary penalty, disbarment, or suspension of six months or longer

cnc.hardship_codes.value: closing codes 24 through 32, available only for individual or joint IMF assessments, sole proprietorships, partnerships where a general partner is personally liable, and LLCs where an individual owner is the liable taxpayer

cnc.nftl_threshold.value: a Notice of Federal Tax Lien should generally be filed on an account reported CNC where the aggregate unpaid balance of assessments is $10,000 or more

cod.1099c_threshold.value: $600 — an applicable entity need not report a discharge of less than that, and this figure was NOT among those raised to $2,000 for 2026

cod.attribute_order.value: seven, in order — net operating loss, general business credit carryovers, minimum tax credit, capital loss carryovers, basis of property, passive activity loss and credit carryovers, foreign tax credit carryovers — at a dollar for each dollar excluded, except 33⅓ cents per dollar against the three credit carryovers

cod.exclusions.value: five — a discharge in a title 11 case, a discharge while insolvent, qualified farm indebtedness, qualified real property business indebtedness for a taxpayer other than a C corporation, and qualified principal residence indebtedness, the last reaching only discharges before 1 January 2026 or under a written arrangement entered into before that date

cod.insolvency_measure.value: the excess of liabilities over the fair market value of assets, determined immediately before the discharge, and the exclusion cannot exceed that amount

combat.disregarded_period.value: the period of service in the combat zone or contingency operation, plus any period of continuous qualified hospitalization attributable to an injury received there, plus the next 180 days

compensation.reasonableness_test.value: whether the payments are reasonable and are in fact payments purely for services — an amount paid as compensation but not in fact as the purchase price of services is not deductible

competence.firm_discipline.value: discipline requires willfulness, recklessness or gross incompetence in failing to ensure adequate procedures exist, or that they are followed, or in failing to take prompt corrective action — together with a pattern or practice of non-compliance by one or more members, associates or employees

competence.firm_procedures.value: an individual with, or sharing, principal authority and responsibility for overseeing a firm's practice must take reasonable steps to ensure the firm has adequate procedures for all members, associates and employees to comply with subparts A, B and C — and where the firm identifies nobody, the IRS may identify who is responsible

competence.prompt_disposition.value: a practitioner may not unreasonably delay the prompt disposition of any matter before the Internal Revenue Service

competence.standard.value: the appropriate level of knowledge, skill, thoroughness and preparation necessary for the matter for which the practitioner is engaged — attainable through various methods, such as consulting with experts in the relevant area or studying the relevant law

conference.submission_days.value: at least 5 business days before the conference for any written protest, brief or other statement the taxpayer or representative wishes considered; additional or supporting facts may follow within a reasonable time after it

conflict.definition.value: 2 — the representation of one client will be directly adverse to another client, or there is a significant risk that representation of one or more clients will be materially limited by the practitioner's responsibilities to another client, a former client or a third person, or by a personal interest of the practitioner

conflict.retention.value: copies of the written consents must be retained for at least 36 months from the date the representation of the affected clients concluded, and must be provided to any IRS officer or employee on request

conflict.waiver.value: 3 conditions — the practitioner reasonably believes they can provide competent and diligent representation to each affected client; the representation is not prohibited by law; and each affected client waives the conflict and gives informed consent, confirmed in writing, at the time the conflict is known, with the written confirmation made within a reasonable period and in no event later than 30 days

constructive.bank_nonlimitations.value: four things the regulation says are NOT substantial limitations for a bank deposit — withdrawal in even multiples, a comparatively small loss of earnings on early withdrawal, a requirement to withdraw part of the deposit itself, and a requirement to give advance notice

constructive.dividend_property.value: money, securities and any other property, but never stock in the distributing corporation or rights to acquire it

constructive.shareholder_loan.value: any below-market loan directly or indirectly between a corporation and any shareholder is within IRC § 7872, subject only to the $10,000 de minimis exception, which itself falls away where a principal purpose is tax avoidance

constructive.test.value: credited to the taxpayer's account, set apart for them, or otherwise made available so they may draw on it at any time — or could have during the year had notice of intention to withdraw been given

contrib.active_participant.value: where the individual or their spouse is an active participant for any part of a plan year ending with or within the taxable year, the dollar limitations are reduced proportionately across a phase-out range

contrib.annual_addition.value: $72,000 for 2026, or 100 percent of the participant's compensation if less — measured on employer contributions, employee contributions and forfeitures together, and applied per employer

contrib.catchup_50.value: $8,000 for an applicable employer plan other than a SIMPLE arrangement, and $4,000 for a SIMPLE — with $3,850 for certain SIMPLE accounts under IRC § 414(v)(2)(B)(iii)

contrib.catchup_60_63.value: $11,250 for an applicable employer plan other than a SIMPLE, and $5,250 for a SIMPLE, for an individual attaining age 60, 61, 62 or 63 during 2026 — neither figure moved for 2026

contrib.compensation_cap.value: $360,000 of annual compensation may be taken into account under IRC §§ 401(a)(17), 404(l), 408(k)(3)(C) and 408(k)(6)(D)(ii) for 2026

contrib.elective_deferral_limit.value: $24,500 for 2026, the same figure applying to elective deferrals under IRC § 402(g)(1) and to deferrals under a § 457(b) plan by force of § 457(e)(15)

contrib.ira_compensation_test.value: the lesser of the deductible amount or the compensation includible in the individual's gross income for the year — so the contribution can never exceed earned income, whatever the dollar limit

contrib.ira_timing.value: a contribution made on account of a taxable year, not later than the time prescribed for filing the return for that year **without** extensions, is deemed made on the last day of that year

contrib.roth_catchup_threshold.value: $150,000 of 2025 wages — above it, catch-up contributions to an applicable employer plan other than a SEP or SIMPLE must be designated Roth contributions for 2026

contrib.sep_not_under_219.value: IRC § 219 does not apply to an employer contribution to a simplified employee pension — the employer's deduction runs through § 404(h) instead, and the contribution does not consume the individual's IRA limit

contrib.sep_threshold.value: $800 of compensation for 2026 — the floor below which an employee need not be covered by a simplified employee pension

contrib.simple_limit.value: $17,000 of salary reduction contributions for 2026, or $18,100 for certain accounts and plans under IRC § 408(p)(2)(E)(i)(I) or (II)

courts.forums.value: 3 — the United States Tax Court, the United States Court of Federal Claims, and the United States District Court for the judicial district where the taxpayer resides or has a principal place of business

courts.frivolous_penalty.value: a penalty not in excess of $25,000, imposed by the Tax Court in its decision where proceedings were instituted or maintained primarily for delay, the taxpayer's position is frivolous or groundless, or the taxpayer unreasonably failed to pursue available administrative remedies

courts.refund_no_response.value: suit may be filed where no written response to a timely refund claim has been received within 6 months from the date the claim was filed

courts.refund_suit_window.value: 2 years from the date of the notice of claim disallowance; Appeals' consideration of a disallowed claim does not extend it, though it may be extended by mutual agreement
courts.refund_suit_window.source: IRS Pub. 5 (Rev. 4-2021), "District Court and the U.S. Court of Federal Claims" — https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p5.pdf

courts.small_tax_case.value: available where neither the deficiency in dispute nor any claimed overpayment exceeds $50,000 for any one taxable year (subtitle A), at the taxpayer's option concurred in by the Tax Court before hearing — the decision is not reviewable in any other court and is not treated as precedent

cp2000.series.value: CP2000, CP2000A, CP2000B, CP2000C, CP2000D and CP2000E
cp2000.series.source: irs.gov, Understanding your CP2000 series notice, opened 2026-08-18

criminal.financial_status.value: the Secretary shall not use financial status or economic reality examination techniques to determine the existence of unreported income unless there is a reasonable indication that unreported income is likely

criminal.omission_duty.value: a practitioner who knows a client has not complied with the revenue laws, or has made an error in or omission from any return, document, affidavit or other paper submitted or executed under them, must advise the client promptly of that fact and of the consequences under the Code and regulations

criminal.referral_bar.value: no summons may be issued, and no § 7604 enforcement action begun, with respect to any person while a Justice Department referral is in effect for that person — each taxable period and each tax imposed by a separate chapter being treated separately

criminal.referral_trigger.value: a referral is in effect once the Secretary has recommended to the Attorney General a grand jury investigation of, or the criminal prosecution of, the person for an offence connected with the administration or enforcement of the internal revenue laws, or once a request is made under § 6103(h)(3)(B) for disclosure of that person's return or return information

csed.abroad.value: suspended while the taxpayer is outside the United States for a continuous period of at least 6 months, and not expiring before 6 months after return

csed.bankruptcy_tail.value: suspended while collection is barred by the bankruptcy case, plus 6 months

csed.cdp_tail.value: suspended while a CDP hearing and appeals are pending, and in no event expiring before the 90th day after a final determination

csed.custody_tail.value: suspended while the taxpayer's assets are in the control or custody of a court, plus 6 months

csed.period.value: 10 years after the assessment of the tax

ctc.amount.value: $2,200 per qualifying child, phasing out above a threshold of $400,000 on a joint return and $200,000 in any other case
ctc.amount.source: Rev. Proc. 2025-32 § 3.05(1); IRC § 24(h)(2), (h)(3) as made permanent by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70104 — https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/24

ctc.other_dependents.value: $500 for each dependent who is not a qualifying child, non-refundable and not indexed

ctc.refundable_portion.value: $1,700 for each qualifying child for taxable years beginning in 2026 — the IRC § 24(h)(5) cap of $1,400 as indexed from 2024 under § 24(i)(1)
ctc.refundable_portion.source: IRC § 24(h) as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70104, read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/24, with Rev. Proc. 2025-32 § 3.05 read at irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/rp-25-32.pdf

ctc.ssn_required.value: the taxpayer's social security number — or, on a joint return, that of at least one spouse — and the social security number of the qualifying child
ctc.ssn_required.source: IRC § 24(h)(7)(A) as amended generally by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70104(b) — https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/24

damages.exclusion.value: damages other than punitive received on account of personal **physical** injuries or physical sickness, reduced by amounts attributable to IRC § 213 medical deductions allowed in a prior year
damages.exclusion.source: IRC § 104(a)(2) and the flush language of § 104(a) — https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/104

datasec.mfa_factors.value: at least two of three authentication factors — a knowledge factor such as a password, a possession factor such as a token, and an inherence factor such as biometric information — required of all companies regardless of size
datasec.mfa_factors.source: Publication 4557, Safeguarding Taxpayer Data — A Guide for Your Business

datasec.online_provider_standards.value: 6 security and privacy standards that Online Providers must follow, set out in Publication 1345
datasec.online_provider_standards.source: Publication 4557, Safeguarding Taxpayer Data — A Guide for Your Business

datasec.password_length.value: a minimum of 8 characters, the NIST standard, with a unique password per user and no sharing
datasec.password_length.source: Publication 4557, Safeguarding Taxpayer Data — A Guide for Your Business

datasec.plan_areas.value: 3 areas the Safeguards Rule identifies as particularly important — employee management and training, information systems, and detecting and managing system failures
datasec.plan_areas.source: Publication 4557, Safeguarding Taxpayer Data — A Guide for Your Business

dcc.applicable_percentage.value: 50 percent, reduced by one point for each $2,000 of adjusted gross income above $15,000 but not below 35 percent, then further reduced by one point for each $2,000 ($4,000 joint) above $75,000 ($150,000 joint) but not below 20 percent
dcc.applicable_percentage.source: IRC § 21(a)(2) as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70405(a), (b) — https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/21

dcc.expense_limit.value: $3,000 of employment-related expenses for one qualifying individual and $6,000 for two or more — neither indexed

decedent.discharge_window.value: the IRS notifies the executor of the amount due within 9 months of the request; on payment, or if no notice issues in that period, the executor is discharged from personal liability

decedent.prompt_assessment.value: 18 months from the date the written request is received, in place of the ordinary 3 years; available for any return of the decedent or the estate except the estate tax return

deduction.charitable_nonitemizer.value: up to $1,000 ($2,000 on a joint return) of cash contributions to a § 170(b)(1)(A) organization other than a supporting organization or donor advised fund

deduction.overtime_cap.value: $12,500 of qualified overtime compensation ($25,000 on a joint return), reduced by $100 for each $1,000 of modified adjusted gross income above $150,000 ($300,000 on a joint return)

deduction.tips_cap.value: $25,000 of qualified tips, reduced by $100 for each $1,000 of modified adjusted gross income above $150,000 ($300,000 on a joint return)

deduction.vehicle_interest_cap.value: $10,000 of interest on a first-lien loan for a personal-use passenger vehicle bought after 31 December 2024, reduced by $200 for each $1,000 of modified adjusted gross income above $100,000 ($200,000 on a joint return), for years before 2029

deferral.correction_dates.value: allocate the excess among the plans by 1 March following the close of the taxable year, and each plan may distribute its allocated share with allocable income by 15 April following that close

deferral.limit.value: $24,500 of elective deferrals for 2026, adjusted from the $15,000 still printed in IRC § 402(g)(1)(B)

deficiency.petition_period.value: 90 days after the notice of deficiency is mailed, or 150 days if addressed to a person outside the United States, not counting a Saturday, Sunday or District of Columbia legal holiday as the last day

dependency.multiple_support.value: the taxpayer must contribute over 10 percent of support, no one person may contribute over half, over half must come from persons who would each otherwise qualify, and every other such person contributing over 10 percent must file a written declaration

dependency.qc_age.value: under 19 at the close of the calendar year, or under 24 if a student, and in either case younger than the taxpayer; any age if permanently and totally disabled at any time during the year

dependency.qc_tests.value: 5 — relationship, the same principal place of abode as the taxpayer for more than half the year, the age requirement, that the individual has not provided over half of their own support, and that the individual has not filed a joint return other than to claim a refund

dependency.qr_gross_income.value: $5,300 — the exemption amount referred to in IRC § 152(d)(1)(B) for taxable years beginning in 2026

dependency.qr_tests.value: 4 — the relationship or member-of-household test, gross income below the exemption amount, support of over one-half provided by the taxpayer, and that the individual is not a qualifying child of the taxpayer or of any other taxpayer

dependency.tiebreak.value: a parent over a non-parent; between parents not filing jointly, the one with whom the child resided longest, then the higher adjusted gross income; where no parent claims, another taxpayer only if their adjusted gross income exceeds the highest of any parent's

dependentcare.exclusion.value: $7,500, or $3,750 on a separate return by a married individual, raised from $5,000 and $2,500 for taxable years beginning after 31 December 2025
dependentcare.exclusion.source: IRC § 129(a)(2)(A) as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70404, read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/129

depletion.independent_producer.value: 15 percent, available only on average daily production up to a tentative depletable quantity of 1,000 barrels of domestic crude oil, and further capped at 65 percent of taxable income computed without oil and gas depletion, the § 199A deduction, or NOL and capital loss carrybacks

depletion.percentage_cap.value: the statutory percentage of gross income from the property, excluding rents and royalties the taxpayer paid on it, capped at 50 percent of taxable income from the property — 100 percent for oil and gas properties

diligence.reliance.value: a practitioner is presumed to have exercised due diligence where they rely on the work product of another person and used reasonable care in engaging, supervising, training and evaluating that person, taking proper account of the nature of the relationship — except as modified by §§ 10.34 and 10.37

diligence.scope.value: 3 — in preparing or assisting in the preparation of, approving, and filing returns, documents, affidavits and other papers relating to IRS matters; in determining the correctness of oral or written representations made to the Treasury Department; and in determining the correctness of oral or written representations made to clients on any matter administered by the IRS

disclosure.6103c_receipt_window.value: 120 days following the date the taxpayer signed and dated the request or consent — the IRS will not make the disclosure if it is received later

disclosure.7216_consent_duration.value: the period the consent document specifies; where it specifies none, 1 year from the date the taxpayer signed it

disclosure.8275_scope.value: discloses items or positions not otherwise adequately disclosed, except those taken contrary to a regulation; it avoids the disregard-of-rules and substantial-understatement portions of the accuracy-related penalty for non-tax-shelter items where the position has a reasonable basis, and may be used for the economic substance disclosure and the preparer penalties
disclosure.8275_scope.source: Instructions for Form 8275 (Rev. 10/2024), "Purpose of Form" — https://www.irs.gov/instructions/i8275

disclosure.8275r_scope.value: discloses positions taken contrary to Treasury regulations; it avoids the disregard-of-regulations and substantial-understatement portions for non-tax-shelter items where the position has a reasonable basis — and cannot avoid the disregard of rules other than regulations, which is Form 8275's territory
disclosure.8275r_scope.source: Instructions for Form 8275-R (Rev. 11/2024), "Purpose of Form" — https://www.irs.gov/instructions/i8275r

disclosure.adequate_standard.value: the position must be adequately disclosed and have at least a reasonable basis; to avoid the disregard-of-regulations portion it must also represent a good-faith challenge to the validity of the regulation — and disclosure cannot cure a failure to keep proper books and records or to substantiate items
disclosure.adequate_standard.source: Instructions for Form 8275 (Rev. 10/2024), "Adequate disclosure"; Reg. § 1.6662-3(c)(1) — https://www.irs.gov/instructions/i8275

disclosure.not_curable.value: negligence; substantial understatement on a tax shelter item; substantial or gross valuation misstatements under chapter 1, including non-arm's-length prices; substantial overstatement of pension liabilities; substantial estate or gift tax valuation understatements; tax benefits from a transaction lacking economic substance under § 7701(o); undisclosed foreign financial asset understatements; inconsistent estate basis; overstatement of the § 170(p) deduction; and disallowance under § 170(h)(7)
disclosure.not_curable.source: Instructions for Form 8275 (Rev. 10/2024) and Form 8275-R (Rev. 11/2024) — https://www.irs.gov/instructions/i8275

disclosure.reasonable_basis.value: a relatively high standard of tax reporting, significantly higher than not frivolous or not patently improper, and not satisfied by a position that is merely arguable; a position reasonably based on an authority in Reg. § 1.6662-4(d)(3)(iii) generally satisfies it even if it does not meet the substantial authority standard
disclosure.reasonable_basis.source: Instructions for Form 8275 (Rev. 10/2024), "Reasonable basis"; Reg. §§ 1.6662-4(d), 1.6662-3(b)(3) — https://www.irs.gov/instructions/i8275

disposition.1099a.value: filed by a lender in a trade or business that acquires an interest in secured property in satisfaction of the debt, or has reason to know it has been abandoned — box 2 the unpaid principal outstanding, box 4 the fair market value, box 5 a checkbox for whether the borrower was personally liable
disposition.1099a.source: IRC § 6050J(a), (b), (c); Instructions for Forms 1099-A and 1099-C, Boxes 2, 4 and 5 — https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1099ac.pdf

disposition.1231_netting.value: where section 1231 gains exceed section 1231 losses for the year, both are long-term capital; where they do not, both are ordinary — but net section 1231 gain is ordinary to the extent of net section 1231 losses from the five most recent preceding years not already recaptured

disposition.amount_realized.value: money received plus the fair market value of any property other than money received, and — except as the regulation provides otherwise — the amount of liabilities from which the transferor is discharged as a result of the disposition

disposition.gain_formula.value: amount realized less adjusted basis for gain; adjusted basis less amount realized for loss — the two are measured against the same basis but stated as separate rules

disposition.nonrecourse.value: the whole liability enters the amount realized, whatever the property is worth — the disposition of property securing a nonrecourse liability discharges the transferor from it, and there is no discharge of indebtedness income

disposition.recourse.value: the amount realized is the property's fair market value, and the debt forgiven above that value is discharge of indebtedness income under IRC § 61(a)(12), tested separately under § 108 — two items, not one

dividend.reporting_floor.value: $10 or more of dividends paid to any person in a calendar year, and the same for a nominee passing dividends on

duedate.calendar_year.value: the 15th day of April following the close of the calendar year

duedate.fiscal_year.value: the 15th day of the fourth month following the close of the fiscal year

duedate.nonresident_alien.value: the 15th day of June following the close of the calendar year, or the 15th day of the sixth month following a fiscal year, for a nonresident alien individual whose wages are not subject to chapter 24 withholding

duediligence.benefits.value: head of household filing status; the child tax credit, additional child tax credit and credit for other dependents under section 24; the American opportunity tax credit; and the earned income credit

duediligence.retention.value: 3 years from the latest of the unextended due date, the e-filing date, the date presented to the taxpayer for signature, or a nonsigning preparer's submission date

ea.ce.contact_hour.value: 50 minutes of continuous participation; credit is granted only for a full contact hour or multiples of it, and a university semester hour equals 15 contact hours while a quarter hour equals 10

ea.ce.hours_per_cycle.value: 72 hours per enrollment cycle including 6 hours of ethics, and a minimum of 16 hours per enrollment year including 2 hours of ethics

ea.ce.instruction_cap.value: 6 hours annually for enrolled agents and enrolled retirement plan agents, and 4 hours annually for registered tax return preparers, counting instruction and preparation together

ea.ce.recordkeeping.value: 4 years following the date of renewal

ea.enrollment_fee.value: $140 to enroll initially, and $140 to renew
ea.enrollment_fee.source: 26 CFR §§ 300.5(b) and 300.6(b), applicable beginning 31 October 2022 (T.D. 9966) — https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/26/300.5 and /300.6

earlydist.general_exceptions.value: nine in IRC § 72(t)(2)(A) — age 59½, death, disability, substantially equal periodic payments, separation from service after attaining age 55, IRC § 404(k) dividends, a IRC § 6331 levy, certain federal phased retirement annuities, and net income withdrawn with a IRC § 408(d)(4) corrective distribution

earlydist.ira_only.value: health insurance premiums of an individual who received unemployment compensation for 12 consecutive weeks, higher education expenses, and first-time home purchase — each drafted to reach distributions from an individual retirement plan

earlydist.newer_exceptions.value: $5,000 per birth or adoption; an emergency personal expense distribution capped at the lesser of $1,000 or the interest above $1,000, one per calendar year; a domestic abuse distribution capped at the lesser of $10,000 or half the nonforfeitable accrued benefit; and terminal illness certified against an 84-month prognosis
earlydist.newer_exceptions.source: IRC § 72(t)(2)(H)(ii), (I), (L)(ii), and the emergency and terminal illness subparagraphs — https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/72

earlydist.not_for_iras.value: the separation-from-service-after-55 exception and the qualified domestic relations order exception do not apply to distributions from an individual retirement plan

earlydist.qualified_plan_sepp.value: for a IRC § 401(a) trust or a IRC § 72(e)(5)(D)(ii) contract, the substantially equal periodic payments exception applies only where the series begins after the employee separates from service

earlydist.sepp_recapture.value: modifying a series of substantially equal periodic payments before the later of five years from the first payment or age 59½ — other than by death, disability or a qualifying distribution — reimposes the tax that would have applied, plus interest for the deferral period

edassist.exclusion.value: $5,250, unchanged for 2026 and first indexed for taxable years beginning after 2026
edassist.exclusion.source: IRC § 127(a)(2), (d)(1) as added by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70412(b) — https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/127

edcredits.phaseout.value: modified adjusted gross income of $80,000, or $160,000 on a joint return — not indexed since the IRC § 25A(h) adjustment was struck in 2020

educator.deduction.value: $350 of the expenses of an eligible educator — a kindergarten through grade 12 teacher, instructor, counselor, principal or aide for at least 900 hours in a school year

efile.1040x.periods.value: the current tax period and the two prior ones

efile.ad_retention.broadcast.value: until the end of the calendar year following the last transmission or use
efile.ad_retention.broadcast.source: Publication 3112, IRS e-file Application and Participation (Rev. 11-2025), Advertising Standards

efile.ad_retention.direct.value: until the end of the calendar year following the date sent
efile.ad_retention.direct.source: Publication 3112, IRS e-file Application and Participation (Rev. 11-2025), Advertising Standards

efile.application_processing.value: up to 45 days for the IRS to approve an application
efile.application_processing.source: Publication 3112, IRS e-file Application and Participation (Rev. 11-2025)

efile.expulsion.reconsideration.value: five years from the date the firm was expelled, or five years after the individual completed rehabilitation
efile.expulsion.reconsideration.source: Publication 3112, IRS e-file Application and Participation (Rev. 11-2025), Sanctioning, Levels of Infractions and Administrative Review Process

efile.large_taxpayer.value: assets of $10 million or more, or a partnership with more than 100 partners
efile.large_taxpayer.source: Publication 3112, IRS e-file Application and Participation (Rev. 11-2025)

efile.logo_clearance.value: no text closer than one quarter of an inch from the logo
efile.logo_clearance.source: Publication 3112, IRS e-file Application and Participation (Rev. 11-2025), Advertising Standards

efile.new_declaration.income.source: Publication 1345, Handbook for Authorized IRS e-file Providers of Individual Income Tax Returns (Rev. 12-2025)

efile.new_declaration.tax.value: $14 to “Total tax,” “Federal income tax withheld,” “Refund” or “Amount you owe”
efile.new_declaration.tax.source: Publication 1345, Handbook for Authorized IRS e-file Providers of Individual Income Tax Returns (Rev. 12-2025)

efile.online_provider_prefixes.source: Publication 3112, IRS e-file Application and Participation (Rev. 11-2025)

efile.perfection.business.value: postmarked by the due date including extensions, or 10 calendar days after the IRS last gives notification the return was rejected
efile.perfection.business.source: Publication 4163, Modernized e-File (MeF) Information for Authorized IRS e-file Providers for Business Returns

efile.perfection.individual.value: the fifth calendar day after the due date of the return
efile.perfection.individual.source: Publication 1345, Handbook for Authorized IRS e-file Providers of Individual Income Tax Returns (Rev. 12-2025)

efile.perfection.individual_paper.value: the later of the due date or 10 calendar days after the IRS notification of rejection
efile.perfection.individual_paper.source: Publication 1345, Handbook for Authorized IRS e-file Providers of Individual Income Tax Returns (Rev. 12-2025)

efile.provider_min_age.value: at least 18 years of age as of the date of application
efile.provider_min_age.source: Publication 3112, IRS e-file Application and Participation (Rev. 11-2025)

efile.reactivation_window.value: 60 days to reply and request reactivation before a new application is required
efile.reactivation_window.source: Publication 3112, IRS e-file Application and Participation (Rev. 11-2025)

efile.reject_notify.source: Publication 1345, Handbook for Authorized IRS e-file Providers of Individual Income Tax Returns (Rev. 12-2025)

efile.review.deadline.value: 30 calendar days from the date of the denial or sanction letter, at each step
efile.review.deadline.source: Publication 3112, IRS e-file Application and Participation (Rev. 11-2025), Sanctioning, Levels of Infractions and Administrative Review Process

efile.sanction.effective.value: 30 days after the date of the letter informing of the sanction, or the date the reviewing office or the Independent Office of Appeals affirms it, whichever is later
efile.sanction.effective.source: Publication 3112, IRS e-file Application and Participation (Rev. 11-2025), Sanctioning, Levels of Infractions and Administrative Review Process

efile.sanction.levels.value: 3 — Level One (little or no adverse impact), Level Two (adverse impact, including a continued Level One infraction after it was brought to the provider's attention), Level Three (significant adverse impact, including a continued Level Two infraction after notice)
efile.sanction.levels.source: Publication 3112, IRS e-file Application and Participation (Rev. 11-2025), Sanctioning, Levels of Infractions and Administrative Review Process

efile.sanction.suspension.value: one or two years from the effective date of the sanction, depending on the severity of the infraction
efile.sanction.suspension.source: Publication 3112, IRS e-file Application and Participation (Rev. 11-2025), Sanctioning, Levels of Infractions and Administrative Review Process

efile.selfselect_pin_ineligible.value: primary taxpayers under age 16 who have never filed, and secondary taxpayers under age 16 who did not file the prior tax year
efile.selfselect_pin_ineligible.source: Publication 1345, Handbook for Authorized IRS e-file Providers of Individual Income Tax Returns (Rev. 12-2025)

efile.sig_auth_retention.value: three years from the return due date or the IRS received date, whichever is later
efile.sig_auth_retention.source: Publication 1345, Handbook for Authorized IRS e-file Providers of Individual Income Tax Returns (Rev. 12-2025)

efile.specified_preparer.threshold.value: a preparer who does not reasonably expect to file 10 or fewer individual income tax returns in the calendar year — that is, 11 or more, counted across the firm

efile.waiver_duration.value: not ordinarily granted for more than a one calendar year period

efile.waiver_window.value: between 1 October of the preceding calendar year and 15 February of the applicable calendar year

eitc.childless_age_range.value: at least 25 and under 65 at the close of the taxable year, tested against either spouse on a joint return, with a principal place of abode in the United States for more than half the year

eitc.earned_income_amount.value: $8,680 with no qualifying child, $13,020 with one, and $18,290 with two or with three or more — the earned income at or above which the maximum credit is reached, for 2026

eitc.investment_income_limit.value: $12,200 — above this aggregate of disqualified investment income no credit is allowed at all

eitc.max_credit.value: $664 with no qualifying child, $4,427 with one, $7,316 with two and $8,231 with three or more, for taxable years beginning in 2026

eitc.phaseout.value: on a joint return the credit begins to phase out at $18,140 with no child or $31,160 with any, ending at $19,540 / $58,863 / $65,899 / $70,244 by number of children; for every other filing status the thresholds are $10,860 and $23,890, ending at $19,540 / $51,593 / $58,629 / $62,974
eitc.phaseout.source: Rev. Proc. 2025-32 § 3.06(1), adjusting IRC § 32(b), including the § 32(b)(2)(B) joint-return increase — https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/rp-25-32.pdf

eitc.tin_required.value: a social security number issued by the Social Security Administration, other than one issued solely for non-work purposes, on or before the due date for filing the return for the taxable year

energy.credit_terminations.value: the residential clean energy credit ends for expenditures made after 31 December 2025, the energy efficient home improvement credit for property placed in service after that date, and the new clean vehicle credit for vehicles acquired after 30 September 2025

entity.default_domestic.value: a partnership if it has two or more members, or disregarded as an entity separate from its owner if it has a single owner

entity.default_foreign.value: a partnership if it has two or more members and at least one member does not have limited liability; an association if all members have limited liability; or disregarded if it has a single owner that does not have limited liability

estimated.de_minimis.value: no addition to tax where the tax shown on the return, reduced by the IRC § 31 withholding credit, is less than $1,000

estimated.installment_share.value: 25 percent of the required annual payment per installment, unless the annualized income installment is lower, in which case the reduction is recaptured in the next installment

estimated.required_annual_payment.value: the lesser of 90 percent of the tax shown on this year's return or 100 percent of the tax shown on last year's, rising to 110 percent where last year's adjusted gross income exceeded $150,000, or $75,000 for a married individual filing separately

evasion.7201.value: a felony — willfully attempting in any manner to evade or defeat any tax or its payment; fine of not more than $100,000 ($500,000 for a corporation) as stated in the section, imprisonment of not more than 5 years, or both, together with the costs of prosecution

evasion.7203.value: a misdemeanor — willful failure to pay estimated tax or tax, file a return, keep records, or supply information when required; fine of not more than $25,000 ($100,000 for a corporation) as stated in the section, imprisonment of not more than 1 year, or both — raised to a felony with 5 years for a willful violation of § 6050I

evasion.7206.value: a felony — willfully signing a return or document verified under penalties of perjury that the signer does not believe true and correct as to every material matter, or willfully aiding or assisting in preparing a materially false or fraudulent document; fine of not more than $100,000 ($500,000 for a corporation) as stated in the section, imprisonment of not more than 3 years, or both

evasion.civil_fraud.value: 75 percent of the portion of the underpayment attributable to fraud; where the Secretary establishes that any portion is attributable to fraud the entire underpayment is so treated, except any portion the taxpayer shows by a preponderance of the evidence is not

evasion.title18_fines.value: the fine is the greatest of the amount in the offense statute or, for a felony, $250,000 for an individual and $500,000 for an organization — so the $100,000 stated in IRC §§ 7201 and 7206 is superseded upward for individuals unless the offense statute exempts itself by specific reference

exam.agreed_interest_grace.value: no further interest or penalty where a balance under $100,000 is paid within 21 calendar days of the bill, reduced to 10 business days where the amount is $100,000 or more

exam.lookback.value: generally returns filed within the last 3 years; additional years may be added where a substantial error is identified, and the IRS usually does not go back more than 6 years — most audits are of returns filed within the last 2 years
exam.lookback.source: IRS, "IRS audits," page last reviewed 17 February 2026 — https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/irs-audits

exam.mail_extension.value: a one-time automatic 30-day extension is ordinarily granted for an audit conducted by mail; no additional time is available once a notice of deficiency has issued, and the 90-day Tax Court petition period cannot be extended
exam.mail_extension.source: IRS, "IRS audits," page last reviewed 17 February 2026 — https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/irs-audits

exam.one_inspection.value: one inspection of a taxpayer's books of account per taxable year, unless the taxpayer requests otherwise or an authorized officer, after investigation, notifies the taxpayer in writing that an additional inspection is necessary

exam.record_retention.value: at least 3 years from the date the return was filed, for all records used to prepare it
exam.record_retention.source: IRS, "IRS audits," page last reviewed 17 February 2026 — https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/irs-audits

exam.summons_appearance_days.value: the date fixed for appearance must be no less than 10 days from the date of the summons

exam.transfer_factors.value: 6 — the taxpayer's current residence; current principal place of business; where the books, records and source documents are maintained; where the Service can examine most efficiently; the Service resources available at the requested location; and other factors showing undue inconvenience

exam.transfer_sol_window.value: where a limitations period on assessment or collection will expire within 13 months of the request, the Service may condition an otherwise permissible transfer on a written extension of up to one year

exam.types.value: by mail (correspondence), or by in-person interview — at an IRS office (office audit) or at the taxpayer's home, place of business, or accountant's or representative's office (field audit)
exam.types.source: IRS, "IRS audits," page last reviewed 17 February 2026 — https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/irs-audits

excess.accounts_covered.value: six kinds of account — individual retirement accounts and annuities, Archer MSAs, IRC § 403(b)(7)(A) custodial accounts, Coverdell education savings accounts, health savings accounts and ABLE accounts

excess.excise_tax.value: 6 percent of the excess contributions determined at the close of the taxable year, capped at 6 percent of the account value at that date — imposed for **each** taxable year the excess remains, and payable by the individual

excess.timely_correction.value: distribution received on or before the due date including extensions, no IRC § 219 deduction taken for the contribution, and the distribution accompanied by the net income attributable — with that net income treated as earned in the year the contribution was made

excessaccum.correction_window.value: from the date the tax is imposed to the earliest of the mailing of a notice of deficiency, the assessment of the tax, or the last day of the second taxable year beginning after the end of the taxable year in which the tax was imposed

excessaccum.excise_tax.value: 25 percent of the amount by which the minimum required distribution exceeds the amount actually distributed during the taxable year, paid by the payee

excessaccum.reduced_rate.value: 10 percent in place of 25, where the shortfall is distributed from the same plan and a return reflecting the tax is filed, both within the correction window
