excessaccum.waiver.value: the Secretary may waive the tax where the taxpayer establishes that the shortfall was due to reasonable error and that reasonable steps are being taken to remedy it — claimed by entering "RC" and the amount on Form 5329 with a statement attached
excessaccum.waiver.source: IRC § 4974(d); Instructions for Form 5329, Waiver of tax for reasonable cause — https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i5329.pdf

exemption.amount.value: zero — and permanently so for taxable years beginning after 2017, following Pub. L. 119-21 § 70103(a)
exemption.amount.source: IRC § 151(d)(5)(A) as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70103(a)(1), (2) — https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/151

exemption.tin_required.value: no exemption is allowed with respect to an individual unless that individual's TIN is included on the return claiming it

extension.abroad.value: to and including the fifteenth day of the sixth month following the close of the taxable year, for a United States citizen or resident whose tax home and abode are outside the United States and Puerto Rico, or who is in military or naval service on duty outside them

extension.automatic_individual.value: an automatic 6-month extension of time to file, on a complete application made on Form 4868 by the date prescribed for filing

extension.pay.bond.value: a bond not exceeding double the amount for which the extension is granted, where the Secretary requires security

extension.pay.deficiency_period.value: not exceeding 18 months from the date fixed for payment of the deficiency, and in exceptional cases a further period not exceeding 12 months

extension.pay.hardship.value: substantial financial loss, not mere inconvenience — a general statement of hardship will not do, and selling property at current market price where a market exists is not ordinarily hardship

extension.pay.return_period.value: a reasonable period not exceeding 6 months from the date fixed for payment, and longer where the taxpayer is abroad; 12 months for estate tax

extension.pay.support.value: Form 1127 with evidence of the hardship, a statement of assets and liabilities, and an itemised statement of all receipts and disbursements for each of the 3 months preceding the due date

f8938.penalty.value: $10,000, plus $10,000 for each 30-day period or fraction of one during which the failure continues more than 90 days after the Secretary mails notice, to a maximum continuation penalty of $50,000

f8938.threshold_abroad.value: exceeding $200,000 on the last day of the taxable year, or $300,000 at any time during the year, for a specified individual who is a qualified individual under IRC § 911(d)(1)

f8938.threshold_joint.value: exceeding $100,000 on the last day of the taxable year, or $150,000 at any time during the year

f8938.threshold_joint_abroad.value: exceeding $400,000 on the last day of the taxable year, or $600,000 at any time during the year

f8938.threshold_single.value: exceeding $50,000 on the last day of the taxable year, or $75,000 at any time during the year

fbar.due_date.value: April 15 following the calendar year reported, with an automatic extension to October 15 that need not be requested
fbar.due_date.source: IRS, Report of Foreign Bank and Financial Accounts (FBAR) (page last reviewed 30 July 2026) — https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/report-of-foreign-bank-and-financial-accounts-fbar

fbar.exclusions.value: 7 categories the IRS lists as not reportable — correspondent or Nostro accounts, accounts owned by a governmental entity, accounts owned by an international financial institution, accounts maintained on a U.S. military banking facility, accounts held in an IRA of which the person is owner or beneficiary, accounts held in a retirement plan of which the person is participant or beneficiary, and accounts held in a trust of which the person is a beneficiary where a U.S. person files an FBAR reporting them
fbar.exclusions.source: IRS, Report of Foreign Bank and Financial Accounts (FBAR) (page last reviewed 30 July 2026) — https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/report-of-foreign-bank-and-financial-accounts-fbar

fbar.filing_threshold.value: an aggregate value greater than $10,000 at any time during the calendar year
fbar.filing_threshold.source: IRM 5.15.1.6, Internal Sources and Online Research (revised 29 June 2026), describing FinCEN Form 114

fbar.threshold.value: an aggregate value of the foreign financial accounts exceeding $10,000 at any time during the calendar year reported
fbar.threshold.source: IRS, Report of Foreign Bank and Financial Accounts (FBAR) (page last reviewed 30 July 2026) — https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/report-of-foreign-bank-and-financial-accounts-fbar

feie.housing.value: housing expenses above 16 percent of the exclusion amount, capped at 30 percent of it, both computed on a daily basis over the qualifying period

feie.qualification.value: a tax home in a foreign country, plus either bona fide residence in a foreign country for an uninterrupted period including an entire taxable year — open to citizens only — or physical presence in foreign countries for at least 330 full days in any 12 consecutive months, open to citizens and residents alike

foia.appeal_window.value: an appeal must be postmarked within 90 days after the date of the denial letter (10 days where expedited processing was denied); the IRS must decide it within 20 days excluding Saturdays, Sundays and legal holidays, extendable by 10
foia.appeal_window.source: 31 CFR Part 1 § 1.6, as described by IRS, "Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) guidelines," page last reviewed 28 June 2026 — https://www.irs.gov/privacy-disclosure/freedom-of-information-act-foia-guidelines

foia.exclusions.value: 3 special protection provisions permitting especially sensitive law enforcement records to be treated as not subject to the FOIA, so that the IRS may respond that there are no responsive records — they apply only to information that is otherwise exempt and do not broaden the authority to withhold
foia.exclusions.source: 5 U.S.C. § 552(c); IRS, "Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) guidelines," page last reviewed 28 June 2026 — https://www.irs.gov/privacy-disclosure/freedom-of-information-act-foia-guidelines

foia.exemptions.value: 9 — classified national defense and foreign policy documents; internal personnel rules and practices; information exempt under other laws; trade secrets and confidential commercial or financial information; inter-agency or intra-agency memorandums or letters; personal privacy; law enforcement; financial institutions; and geological information
foia.exemptions.source: 5 U.S.C. § 552(b)(1)–(9), as described by IRS, "Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) guidelines," page last reviewed 28 June 2026 — https://www.irs.gov/privacy-disclosure/freedom-of-information-act-foia-guidelines

foia.response_window.value: 20 days, excluding Saturdays, Sundays and legal public holidays, from receipt of the request, extendable by 10 additional days in unusual circumstances of which the requester must be notified
foia.response_window.source: 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(6); Reg. § 601.702(c)(11)(i)(A)(1)–(4); IRS FOIA guidelines, last reviewed 28 June 2026 — https://www.irs.gov/privacy-disclosure/freedom-of-information-act-foia-guidelines

foia.segregability.value: any reasonably segregable portion must be provided after the exempt portions are deleted, with the amount deleted and the exemption relied on indicated on the released record — and, where technically feasible, at the place on the record where the deletion was made — unless that indication would itself harm the protected interest

foreignpension.402b_contributions.value: employer contributions to a trust not exempt under IRC § 501(a) are included in the employee's gross income under IRC § 83, substituting the value of the employee's interest in the trust for the fair market value of property — so vesting, not distribution, is the taxing event

foreignpension.402b_distributions.value: taxed to the distributee under IRC § 72 in the year distributed or made available, except that income of the trust distributed before the annuity starting date is included without regard to § 72(e)(5)

foreignpension.402b_hce.value: a highly compensated employee includes the whole vested accrued benefit, less investment in the contract, as of the close of the trust's taxable year — in place of the ordinary § 402(b)(1) and (2) amounts

foreignpension.fbar.value: required of a United States person with a financial interest in or signature authority over foreign financial accounts exceeding $10,000 in the aggregate at any time during the calendar year; the exception for retirement plans reaches only §§ 401(a), 403(a), 403(b), 408 and 408A arrangements

foreignpension.fbar_due.value: 15 April following the calendar year reported, with an automatic extension to 15 October that need not be requested — filed electronically with FinCEN, not with the return
foreignpension.fbar_due.source: IRS, Report of Foreign Bank and Financial Accounts (FBAR), "When to file" — https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/report-of-foreign-bank-and-financial-accounts-fbar

foreignpension.feie.value: unavailable — foreign earned income does not include amounts received as a pension or annuity, nor amounts included in gross income by reason of IRC § 402(b) or § 403(c)

foreignpension.foreign_social_security.value: outside IRC § 86 entirely — a social security benefit for that section means a monthly benefit under title II of the Social Security Act or a tier 1 railroad retirement benefit, so a foreign state pension is ordinary income unless a treaty says otherwise

foreignpension.form3520.value: a United States person treated as owner of any portion of a foreign trust must report under IRC § 6048(b), on pain of a penalty under § 6677(a) of the greater of $10,000 or 35 percent of the gross reportable amount, plus $10,000 per 30 days after notice

foreignpension.form8938.value: required where specified foreign financial assets exceed $50,000 on the last day of the year or $75,000 at any time — $200,000 and $300,000 for a taxpayer living abroad — with a $10,000 penalty rising by $10,000 per 30 days after notice, capped at $50,000

foreignpension.ftc.value: a citizen or resident may credit income, war profits and excess profits taxes paid or accrued to a foreign country, subject to the IRC § 904 limitation

foreignpension.gross_income.value: included — pensions are gross income under IRC § 61(a)(11), and a foreign arrangement has no qualified status to displace that; the plan's treatment in its own country is irrelevant to the United States charge

foreignpension.revproc_relief.value: an eligible individual is exempt from the IRC § 6048 reporting for an applicable tax-favored foreign retirement trust — but the relief expressly does not affect reporting under § 6038D or any other provision, including the FBAR

foreignpension.treaty.value: the Code is applied with due regard to any treaty obligation of the United States applying to the taxpayer, and neither a treaty nor a statute has preferential status merely by being one or the other — the later in time prevails

fraud.7201.sentence.value: a felony: a fine of up to $100,000 ($500,000 for a corporation), imprisonment of up to 5 years, or both, plus costs of prosecution

fraud.assessment_period.value: no limitation period — tax may be assessed at any time on a false or fraudulent return filed with intent to evade

fraud.civil.standard.value: clear and convincing evidence, the burden resting on the government

fraud.criminal.standard.value: beyond a reasonable doubt, the burden resting on the government

fraud.ftf.rate.value: 15% of the tax per month or part month, maximum 75%

frivolous.positions.count.value: 46 numbered positions, each covering positions that are the same as or similar to it
frivolous.positions.count.source: Notice 2010-33, § III (effective for submissions made and issues raised after 7 April 2010)

frivolous.tax_court_penalty.value: up to $25,000 imposed by the Tax Court, and up to $10,000 in a section 7433 proceeding in another court

frivolous.withdrawal_window.value: 30 days after the IRS notifies the person that a submission is a specified frivolous submission

ftc.carryover.value: one year back and ten years forward, in that order, usable only as a credit and never as a deduction, and only for a year in which the taxpayer elects the credit (IRC § 904(c))

ftc.de_minimis_election.value: creditable foreign taxes of $300, or $600 on a joint return, where all foreign source gross income is qualified passive income shown on a payee statement — the taxpayer elects out of the § 904(a) limitation entirely, and forfeits any carryback or carryover for that year (IRC § 904(j))

gambling.expenses_as_losses.value: losses from wagering transactions include any deduction otherwise allowable that is incurred in carrying on a wagering transaction — a rule that ran only from 2018 to 2025 and is now permanent
gambling.expenses_as_losses.source: IRC § 165(d)(2) as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70114(a) — https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/165

gambling.loss_limit.value: 90 percent of wagering losses for the year, and then only to the extent of gains from wagering transactions — both limits applying for the first time to taxable years beginning after 31 December 2025
gambling.loss_limit.source: IRC § 165(d)(1)(A), (B) as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70114(a), (b) — https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/165

gambling.w2g_threshold.value: $2,000 of winnings for calendar year 2026, replacing the former fixed figures for bingo, keno, slot machines and other wagering, and adjusted for inflation for calendar years after 2026
gambling.w2g_threshold.source: IRC § 6041(a), (h) as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70433(a), (e), (f); Instructions for Forms W-2G and 5754 (Rev. January 2026) — https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/iw2g.pdf

gambling.withholding_rate.value: regular gambling withholding at 24 percent, 31.58 percent for certain noncash payments, with backup withholding also at 24 percent
gambling.withholding_rate.source: Instructions for Forms W-2G and 5754 (Rev. January 2026), Withholding; IRC § 3402(q)(1) — https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/iw2g.pdf

gambling.withholding_trigger.value: proceeds of more than $5,000 from a wagering transaction where the proceeds are at least 300 times the amount wagered, with separate rules for State-conducted lotteries, sweepstakes, wagering pools and pari-mutuel pools

gift.annual_exclusion.value: the first $19,000 of gifts to any person, other than gifts of future interests, which are never covered however small

gift.foreign_gift_reporting.value: aggregate gifts from certain foreign persons above $20,573 received in the taxable year

gift.noncitizen_spouse_exclusion.value: $194,000 of gifts to a spouse who is not a United States citizen, again excluding future interests

guidance.reg_retroactivity.value: no temporary, proposed or final regulation applies to a taxable period ending before the earliest of the date it is filed with the Federal Register, the date a related proposed or temporary regulation was so filed, or the date a notice substantially describing its expected contents was issued — with exceptions for regulations issued within 18 months of the statute, to prevent abuse, to correct a procedural defect, for internal Treasury policies, on congressional authorization, and by taxpayer election

guidance.retroactivity.value: revenue rulings apply retroactively unless the ruling states, under IRC § 7805(b), the extent to which it is to apply without retroactive effect — an affirmative act; where a ruling revokes or modifies an earlier published one, § 7805(b) is ordinarily invoked so the new ruling is not applied retroactively to a taxpayer's detriment

guidance.revenue_procedure.value: a statement of procedure affecting the rights or duties of taxpayers or other members of the public under the Code and related statutes, or information that should be a matter of public knowledge although not necessarily affecting those rights and duties

guidance.revenue_ruling.value: an official interpretation by the Service published in the Internal Revenue Bulletin, issued only by the National Office, for the information and guidance of taxpayers, IRS officials and others concerned

guidance.ruling_reliance.value: taxpayers generally may rely on published revenue rulings and need not request a specific ruling applying their principles — but each ruling states the Service's conclusion on the entire state of facts involved, so the same conclusion should not be reached in another case unless the facts and circumstances are substantially the same, and the effect of subsequent legislation, regulations, court decisions and revenue rulings must be considered

guidance.ruling_weight.value: revenue rulings do not have the force and effect of Treasury regulations, but are published to provide precedents to be used in disposing of other cases and may be cited and relied on for that purpose — while no unpublished ruling or decision may be relied on, used or cited as a precedent by any IRS officer or employee

hobby.presumption.value: gross income exceeding deductions in 3 or more of the 5 consecutive taxable years ending with the current year, or 2 of 7 where the activity consists in major part of breeding, training, showing or racing horses

household.fica_threshold.value: $3,000 of cash wages paid to any one household employee in 2026 — the IRC § 3121(x) applicable dollar threshold as adjusted by the Commissioner of Social Security and rounded down to a multiple of $100
household.fica_threshold.source: IRS Topic no. 756, Employment taxes for household employees, read at irs.gov/taxtopics/tc756

household.futa.value: more than $1,000 of cash wages to household employees in any calendar quarter of the year or the prior year triggers federal unemployment tax on the first $7,000 of cash wages per employee, at 6 percent less a credit of up to 5.4 percent for state unemployment contributions — a net 0.6 percent, paid by the employer and never withheld
household.futa.source: IRS Topic no. 756, Employment taxes for household employees, read at irs.gov/taxtopics/tc756

hsa.contribution_limit.value: $4,400 for self-only coverage and $8,750 for family coverage, plus an unindexed $1,000 for an individual who has attained age 55 before the close of the taxable year

hsa.deductible_safe_harbours.value: a plan does not fail to be a high deductible health plan for having no deductible for telehealth and other remote care, for providing surprise-billing benefits before the deductible is met, or for certain insulin products

hsa.dependent_denied.value: no deduction for an individual with respect to whom another taxpayer is allowed a deduction under IRC § 151 for a taxable year beginning in the same calendar year

hsa.distributions.value: not includible where used exclusively for qualified medical expenses; otherwise includible in the beneficiary's gross income, with the tax increased by 20 percent of the amount included

hsa.eligible_individual.value: covered under a high deductible health plan on the first day of the month, and not also covered by any health plan that is not a high deductible plan and provides any benefit the high deductible plan covers

hsa.excess_returned.value: an excess contribution withdrawn with its net income by the due date of the return, including extensions, escapes the inclusion rule

hsa.hdhp.value: an annual deductible of at least $1,700 for self-only or $3,400 for family coverage, with annual out-of-pocket expenses not exceeding $8,500 or $17,000 respectively

hsa.last_month_rule.value: an individual eligible in the last month of the year is treated as eligible for every month of it — but failing to remain eligible through the testing period adds the excess to gross income and imposes a further 10 percent tax, unless the failure is by death or disability

hsa.married_rule.value: where either spouse has family coverage, both are treated as having only that coverage — the family limit is then divided equally between them unless they agree otherwise, with each spouse's catch-up amount left out of the division

hsa.medicare_zero.value: the monthly limitation is zero for the first month the individual is entitled to Medicare benefits and every month after — entitlement, not merely eligibility, ends contributions

hsa.monthly_limitation.value: one twelfth of the annual figure for each month the individual is an eligible individual — so the limit is built month by month rather than allowed for the year

hsa.new_hdhp_categories.value: a bronze or catastrophic plan available as individual coverage through an Exchange is a high deductible health plan, and a direct primary care service arrangement is not a health plan that disqualifies the individual — both added by Pub. L. 119-21
hsa.new_hdhp_categories.source: IRC § 223(c)(2)(H) as added by Pub. L. 119-21 § 71307(a); § 223(c)(1)(E) as added by § 71308(a) — https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/223

hsa.penalty_exceptions.value: the additional tax does not apply to a distribution made after the beneficiary becomes disabled within IRC § 72(m)(7) or dies, or after attaining the age specified in section 1811 of the Social Security Act

hsa.qualified_expenses.value: amounts paid for medical care within IRC § 213(d) for the beneficiary, spouse and dependents, only to the extent not compensated by insurance — including menstrual care products, but **not** payments for insurance itself

ia.setup_fee.lowincome.value: waived with direct debit; $43 otherwise, reimbursed on completion
ia.setup_fee.lowincome.source: IRS Payment plans (installment agreements) page, updated 2026-03-03; ceiling set by Reg. § 300.1(b); IRC § 6159(f)

ia.setup_fee.online_directdebit.source: IRS Payment plans (installment agreements) page, updated 2026-03-03; ceiling set by Reg. § 300.1(b)

ia.setup_fee.online_other.source: IRS Payment plans (installment agreements) page, updated 2026-03-03; ceiling set by Reg. § 300.1(b)

ia.setup_fee.phone_mail_directdebit.source: IRS Payment plans (installment agreements) page, updated 2026-03-03; ceiling set by Reg. § 300.1(b)

ia.setup_fee.phone_mail_other.source: IRS Payment plans (installment agreements) page, updated 2026-03-03; ceiling set by Reg. § 300.1(b)

ia.short_term.fee.source: IRS Payment plans (installment agreements) page, updated 2026-03-03; ceiling set by Reg. § 300.1(b)

ia.short_term.max_days.source: IRS Payment plans (installment agreements) page, updated 2026-03-03; ceiling set by Reg. § 300.1(b)

ia.simple.threshold.value: $50,000 or less aggregate unpaid balance of assessment

idtheft.dependent_efile.value: beginning with 2024 tax returns the IRS accepts e-filed Forms 1040, 1040-NR and 1040-SS even where a dependent has already been claimed on another return, provided the primary taxpayer on the second return includes a valid IP PIN — the dependent needs no IP PIN unless one was previously issued
idtheft.dependent_efile.source: IRS, "Identity theft guide for individuals," page last reviewed 4 June 2026 — https://www.irs.gov/newsroom/taxpayer-guide-to-identity-theft

idtheft.ippin_delivery.value: a confirmed victim enrolled by the IRS receives a CP01A Notice with the new IP PIN each year; a taxpayer who opted in and obtained the IP PIN online must retrieve it online each year, because no CP01A is mailed
idtheft.ippin_delivery.source: IRS, "Get an identity protection PIN," page last reviewed 4 August 2026 — https://www.irs.gov/identity-theft-fraud-scams/get-an-identity-protection-pin

idtheft.ippin_forms.source: IRS, Get an identity protection PIN (page last reviewed or updated 4 August 2026) — https://www.irs.gov/identity-theft-fraud-scams/get-an-identity-protection-pin

idtheft.ippin_online_window.value: generally viewable in the online account from mid-January through mid-November
idtheft.ippin_online_window.source: IRS, Get an identity protection PIN (page last reviewed or updated 4 August 2026) — https://www.irs.gov/identity-theft-fraud-scams/get-an-identity-protection-pin

idtheft.ippin_routes.value: 3 — through the IRS online account (fastest; required for anyone aged 18 or over who can validate identity online); by Form 15227 where adjusted gross income on the last filed return is below $84,000, or $168,000 for married filing jointly, with identity validated by telephone and the IP PIN mailed in about four to six weeks; or by an in-person appointment at a Taxpayer Assistance Center with two forms of identification, with the IP PIN mailed in about three weeks
idtheft.ippin_routes.source: IRS, "Get an identity protection PIN," page last reviewed 4 August 2026 — https://www.irs.gov/identity-theft-fraud-scams/get-an-identity-protection-pin

idtheft.ippin_validity.value: a six-digit number valid for one calendar year, with a new one generated each year; it is used only on Forms 1040, 1040-NR, 1040-PR, 1040-SR and 1040-SS, must be used on any federal return filed during the year including prior-year returns, and is generally viewable in the online account from mid-January through mid-November
idtheft.ippin_validity.source: IRS, Get an identity protection PIN (page last reviewed or updated 4 August 2026) — https://www.irs.gov/identity-theft-fraud-scams/get-an-identity-protection-pin

idtheft.steps.value: stop interacting with the thief; update the Online Account password; follow the instructions in the IRS letter or notice; report the theft and follow the recovery steps at IdentityTheft.gov; get an IP PIN; keep records of letters, calls and emails; file returns and pay tax as usual; and check with the state tax agency
idtheft.steps.source: IRS, "Identity theft guide for individuals," page last reviewed 4 June 2026 — https://www.irs.gov/newsroom/taxpayer-guide-to-identity-theft

income.61_items.value: fourteen, from compensation for services through income from an interest in an estate or trust — a list expressly not exhaustive, and one item shorter since alimony was struck for post-2018 instruments

info.1099k_threshold.value: more than $20,000 in aggregate payments and more than 200 transactions, both required, restored retroactively as if the $600 threshold had never been enacted

info.6041_threshold.value: $2,000 or more of reportable payments in a calendar year, adjusted for inflation for calendar years after 2026
info.6041_threshold.source: IRC § 6041(a), (h) as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70433(a), (e), (f) — https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/6041

info.6041a_threshold.value: remuneration for services equal to or exceeding the dollar amount in effect for the calendar year under IRC § 6041(a) — so the nonemployee compensation threshold now tracks the general one automatically instead of naming its own figure
info.6041a_threshold.source: IRC § 6041A(a)(2) as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70433(c) — https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/6041A

info.direct_sales_threshold.value: $5,000 or more of consumer products sold to a buyer for resale other than in a permanent retail establishment — a separate figure that was NOT changed and does not track IRC § 6041(a)

info.reasonable_cause.value: no penalty under the information reporting part where the failure is shown to be due to reasonable cause and not to wilful neglect

info.tip_reporting_addition.value: payer statements must now separately account for amounts reasonably designated as cash tips and the IRC § 224(d)(1) occupation of the recipient — added to IRC § 6041(f)(2), § 6041A(a), § 6050W(f)(2) and § 6051(a)(18)
info.tip_reporting_addition.source: IRC § 6041A(a) as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70201(f)(2)(A) — https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/6041A

infopenalty.6721.value: $340 per return, reduced to $60 if corrected within 30 days and $130 if corrected by 1 August, with annual caps that differ by the filer's gross receipts — the amounts for returns required to be filed in 2027

inherited.annual_and_outer_limit.value: where the employee died on or after the required beginning date, annual distributions continue for every year until the interest is fully distributed and the ten-year outer limit applies as well — both requirements, not a choice between them

inherited.beneficiary_date.value: the beneficiary is fixed as of the date of death, but a disclaimer or other disregarding event occurring by 30 September of the calendar year following the year of death removes that person from the determination

inherited.edb_categories.value: the surviving spouse; a child of the employee who has not reached majority; a disabled individual within § 72(m)(7); a chronically ill individual within § 7702B(c)(2) as modified; and anyone not more than 10 years younger than the employee

inherited.edb_tested_at_death.value: determined as of the date of the employee's death — a beneficiary who becomes disabled, or who ages past the 10-year gap, afterwards does not change category

inherited.five_year_rule.value: still the rule where there is no designated beneficiary at all — the entire interest by the end of the calendar year containing the fifth anniversary of death

inherited.ird.value: the account is income in respect of a decedent, taxed to whoever receives it in the year received; IRC § 1014 does not apply, so there is no step-up, and a § 691(c) deduction is allowed for the federal estate tax attributable to it

inherited.majority.value: an individual reaches the age of majority on their 21st birthday, after which a minor-child beneficiary ceases to be an eligible designated beneficiary and the remainder must be distributed within 10 years of that date

inherited.no_rollover.value: an inherited IRA — one acquired by reason of another individual's death by someone who was not their surviving spouse — cannot be rolled over and cannot be used to make any other rollover; a non-spouse beneficiary of an employer plan may only take a direct trustee-to-trustee transfer

inherited.roth.value: the requirement attaches after the owner's death, and the Roth IRA owner is always treated as having died before the required beginning date — so the ten-year rule or life expectancy payments, never the at-least-as-rapidly rule

inherited.spouse_delay.value: where the surviving spouse is sole beneficiary, life expectancy payments may be delayed until the end of the calendar year in which the employee would have attained the applicable age

inherited.spouse_own.value: a surviving spouse who is sole beneficiary with an unlimited right to withdraw may elect to treat the account as their own, by redesignation or by deemed election, and is then the owner for all purposes of the Code including § 72(t)

inherited.ten_year_rule.value: the entire interest must be distributed by the end of the calendar year that includes the tenth anniversary of the employee's death — the § 401(a)(9)(B)(ii) five-year rule with ten years substituted

inherited.year_of_death.value: a required distribution is due for the calendar year of the owner's death, and to the extent it was not distributed to the owner it must be distributed during that year to the beneficiary

installment.default.value: automatic — income from an installment sale is taken into account under the installment method unless the taxpayer elects out

installment.definition.value: a disposition of property where at least one payment is to be received after the close of the taxable year of the disposition — a single deferred payment is enough

installment.depreciable_to_controlled.value: the method is unavailable on an installment sale of depreciable property between related persons — all payments to be received are treated as received in the year of disposition

installment.disposition_of_obligation.value: satisfying an installment obligation at other than face value, or selling, distributing or otherwise disposing of it, produces gain or loss measured against the obligation's basis — treated as from the sale of the property for which the obligation was received

installment.exclusions.value: dealer dispositions — personal property sold on the installment plan by a person who regularly does so, and real property held for sale to customers — and inventories of personal property, are outside the method entirely

installment.interest_charge.value: interest is payable on the deferred tax liability where the sales price exceeds $150,000, but only for a year in which the face amount of such obligations arising that year and outstanding at year end exceeds $5,000,000 — and the charge applies to the excess over that figure

installment.method.value: the income recognised for a year is the proportion of the payments received that year which the gross profit, realised or to be realised when payment is complete, bears to the total contract price

installment.pledging.value: pledging an installment obligation to which IRC § 453A applies is treated as a payment on it — the loan proceeds accelerate the gain

installment.recapture_first.value: recapture income is recognised in full in the year of disposition notwithstanding the method, and only the gain in excess of it goes on the installment method — recapture income being what §§ 1245 and 1250 would produce if all payments were received that year

installment.related_party_ordinary.value: gain on a sale between related persons is ordinary income where the property is depreciable in the transferee's hands under IRC § 167

installment.related_second_disposition.value: where a related person disposes of the property before the first seller has been paid in full, the amount realised on that second disposition is treated as received by the first seller at that time

installment.two_year_cutoff.value: the acceleration applies only where the second disposition is within 2 years of the first, except for marketable securities where there is no cutoff — and the 2 years are suspended while the related person's risk of loss is substantially diminished by a put, a short position or a similar arrangement

interest.6404e_erroneous_refund_cap.value: the Secretary shall abate all interest on an erroneous refund until demand for repayment is made, unless the taxpayer or a related party caused it or the refund exceeds $50,000

interest.6404g_suspension.value: 36 months from the later of the filing date or the unextended due date, for a timely-filed individual subtitle A return; the suspension period runs from the day after that until 21 days after the IRS provides the notice

interest.6404h_tax_court_window.value: an action may be brought after the earlier of the final determination not to abate or 180 days from filing the claim, and no later than 180 days after the final determination is mailed

interest.acquisition_cap.value: $750,000, or $375,000 for a married individual filing separately, substituted for the $1,000,000 and $500,000 figures in the statute — with debt incurred on or before 15 December 2017 kept on the higher limit and reducing the lower one

interest.acquisition_indebtedness.value: debt incurred in acquiring, constructing or substantially improving a qualified residence and secured by it, including a refinancing to the extent it does not exceed the refinanced amount

interest.gatt_threshold.value: $10,000 — the part of a corporate overpayment above it takes the federal short-term rate plus 0.5 percentage point

interest.home_equity.value: no deduction — IRC § 163(h)(3)(A)(ii) is disapplied for taxable years beginning after 2017, and Pub. L. 119-21 § 70108(a)(1)(A) struck the end date, so the disallowance is now permanent
interest.home_equity.source: IRC § 163(h)(3)(F)(i)(I), as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70108(a)(1)(A) — https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/163

interest.investment_interest_definition.value: interest on debt properly allocable to property held for investment, excluding qualified residence interest and interest taken into account in computing income or loss from a passive activity

interest.mortgage_insurance.value: premiums for qualified mortgage insurance in connection with acquisition indebtedness are treated as qualified residence interest again — Pub. L. 119-21 § 70108(a)(1)(B) disapplies the § 163(h)(3)(E)(iv) termination that had ended the treatment after 2021

interest.mortgage_insurance_phaseout.value: reduced by 10 percent for each $1,000, or $500 for a married individual filing separately, or fraction thereof by which adjusted gross income exceeds $100,000, or $50,000 filing separately

interest.notice_demand_grace.value: 21 calendar days after notice and demand, or 10 business days where the amount equals or exceeds $100,000 — interest is not imposed for the period after the notice on an amount paid within it

interest.personal_disallowed.value: no deduction for personal interest — defined as any otherwise deductible interest other than trade or business interest, investment interest, passive activity interest, qualified residence interest, deferred estate tax interest, education loan interest and qualified passenger vehicle loan interest

interest.qualified_residence.value: the taxpayer's principal residence within IRC § 121 and **one** other residence selected for the year and used as a residence within § 280A(d)(1) — a third home never qualifies

interest.rate_formula.value: the federal short-term rate plus 3 percentage points for underpayments and for non-corporate overpayments; plus 2 points for a corporate overpayment, reduced to 0.5 point on the part exceeding $10,000; plus 5 points for a large corporate underpayment

interest.rates_q3_2026.value: third quarter 2026: underpayment (corporate and non-corporate) 7%; non-corporate overpayment 7%; corporate overpayment 6%; GATT rate on a corporate overpayment exceeding $10,000, 4.5%; large corporate underpayment 9%; IRC § 6603 deposit (federal short-term) 4%
interest.rates_q3_2026.source: IRS, "Quarterly interest rates," 2026 rates by category, page last reviewed 2 July 2026 (3rd quarter rates per Internal Revenue Bulletin 2026-22) — https://www.irs.gov/payments/quarterly-interest-rates

interest.reporting_floor.value: $10 or more of interest paid to any person in a calendar year, and the same for a nominee passing interest on

interest.short_window_threshold.value: $100,000 — the statute says "equals or exceeds," so the short window applies at exactly that amount

interest.suspension_36_months.value: 36 months from the later of the filing date or the unextended due date, for an individual who filed on time, after which interest and time-sensitive penalties are suspended until 21 days after the IRS gives notice

interest.vehicle_loan.value: for taxable years beginning after 2024 and before 2029, interest on debt incurred after 31 December 2024 to purchase an applicable passenger vehicle for personal use, secured by a first lien on it, is not personal interest — the vehicle identification number must be on the return

interest.vehicle_loan_limits.value: capped at $10,000 of interest, reduced by $200 for each $1,000 or fraction of modified adjusted gross income above $100,000, or $200,000 on a joint return — and excluding fleet, commercial, lease, salvage and scrap financing

intl.6038_penalty.value: $10,000 for each annual accounting period, plus a further $10,000 for each 30-day period beginning 90 days after the Service mails notice, capped at $50,000 of continuation penalty

intl.6677_penalty.value: the greater of $10,000 or 35 percent of the gross reportable amount, with a further penalty if the failure continues more than 90 days after notice

ira.active_participant_phaseout.value: $81,000 to $91,000 for a single active participant; $129,000 to $149,000 on a joint return where the contributing spouse is an active participant; $242,000 to $252,000 where only the other spouse is; and an unindexed $0 to $10,000 for a married active participant filing separately

ira.aggregation_rule.value: all individual retirement plans are treated as one contract, all distributions in a year as one distribution, and the contract value, income and investment are computed at the close of the calendar year in which the taxable year begins — with the value increased by distributions made during that year

ira.deduction_limit.value: $7,500, plus a further $1,100 for an individual who has attained age 50 before the close of the taxable year

ira.early_distribution_tax.value: 10 percent of the portion of the distribution includible in gross income, subject to the exceptions in IRC § 72(t)(2)

ira.first_time_homebuyer.value: a lifetime aggregate of $10,000, used within 120 days of receipt for qualified acquisition costs of a principal residence of the individual, a spouse, or a child, grandchild or ancestor of either

ira.form8606_penalties.value: $50 for each failure to file the form required under IRC § 408(o)(4), and $100 for each overstatement of designated nondeductible contributions — both excused on a showing of reasonable cause

ira.nondeductible_limit.value: the excess of the IRC § 219 deduction computed without regard to § 219(g) over the deduction computed with regard to it — increased by any deductible amount the taxpayer elects not to deduct

ira.qcd_limit.value: $111,000 of qualified charitable distributions for the taxable year, indexed from the $100,000 still printed in IRC § 408(d)(8)(A), and reduced by post-70½ IRC § 219 deductions not already counted

ira.roth_aggregation.value: IRC § 408(d)(2) is applied separately to Roth IRAs and to other individual retirement plans, so a Roth is never blended into the traditional pro-rata computation

ira.spousal_limit.value: the lesser of the individual deduction limit or the couple's combined includible compensation reduced by the other spouse's deduction, designated nondeductible contributions and Roth contributions — so each spouse has a separate limit, not a joint one

irm.definition.value: the single official source of instructions to staff — based on and including the policies, delegated authorities, procedures, instructions and guidelines relating to the organization, functions, administration and operations of the IRS

irm.efoia.value: 3 conditions — the guidance must be procedural and communicate directions, guidelines or standards to employees in performing their duties; affect how a member of the public files, pays, complies or interacts with the IRS; and not be exempt under 5 U.S.C. § 552(b)
irm.efoia.source: IRM 1.11.1.3.1.2 (24 April 2014), "E-FOIA Criteria for Instructions to Staff" — https://www.irs.gov/irm/part1/irm_01-011-001

irm.interim_guidance.value: used to convey new, changed, pilot or temporary procedure, or a deviation from procedure, where there is insufficient time to update and publish the IRM — so an IRM section can be current on its face and superseded by an interim guidance memorandum

irm.ouo.value: instructions to staff affecting the public must be made public unless exempt under 5 U.S.C. § 552(b); generally only § 552(b)(7)(E) applies — content whose disclosure could reasonably be expected to risk circumvention of the law, designated official use only and redacted before posting, with the remaining content accessible
irm.ouo.source: IRM 1.11.1.3.1.3 (7 October 2022), "Disclosure Exemptions for Instructions to Staff" — https://www.irs.gov/irm/part1/irm_01-011-001

irm.parts.value: the parts most used in representation are 4 Examining Process, 5 Collecting Process, 8 Appeals, 13 Taxpayer Advocate Service, 20 Penalty and Interest, 21 Customer Account Services and 25 Special Topics; parts 30 to 39 are the Chief Counsel Directives Manual
irm.parts.source: IRS, "Internal Revenue Manual" table of contents — https://www.irs.gov/irm

itemized.charitable_floor.value: only contributions above 0.5 percent of the taxpayer's contribution base, applied for taxable years beginning after 31 December 2025

itemized.haircut.value: itemized deductions reduced by 2/37 of the lesser of those deductions or the taxable income above the point where the 37 percent bracket begins, first applying to taxable years beginning after 31 December 2025

itemized.medical_floor.value: expenses above 7.5 percent of adjusted gross income

itemized.mortgage_cap.value: $750,000 of acquisition indebtedness ($375,000 on a married filing separate return), with debt incurred on or before 15 December 2017 still measured against the older $1,000,000 limit

itemized.salt_cap.value: $40,400 for taxable years beginning in calendar year 2026 (half that on a married filing separate return), rising 1 percent a year through 2029 and reverting to $10,000 for years beginning after 2029

itemized.salt_threshold.value: $505,000 of modified adjusted gross income for 2026 (half that on a married filing separate return), above which the cap falls by 30 cents on the dollar but never below $10,000

kiddie.age_test.value: a child who has not attained age 18 before the close of the year, or who has attained 18 and meets the § 152(c)(3) age requirement while having earned income not exceeding one-half of their own support

kiddie.base_amount.value: $1,350 — the amount in IRC § 1(g)(4)(A)(ii)(I) for taxable years beginning in 2026, the same figure as the § 63(c)(5)(A) dependent standard deduction floor

kiddie.election_conditions.value: 4 — the child's gross income is only from interest and dividends, it falls within the stated range, no estimated tax payments or backup withholding stand in the child's name and TIN, and the parent elects

kiddie.parental_election_range.value: the child's gross income must be more than $1,350 and less than $13,500 — more than the § 1(g)(4)(A)(ii)(I) amount and less than ten times it

kiddie.threshold.value: $2,700 of unearned income before any is taxed at the parent's rate — twice the § 1(g)(4)(A)(ii)(I) amount, being that amount plus the greater of it or directly connected itemized deductions

levy.continuous.federal_payments.value: up to 15% of a specified federal payment, continuous until released

levy.demand_days.value: 10 days after notice and demand, unless collection is in jeopardy

levy.exempt.household.value: $11,980 of fuel, provisions, furniture, household personal effects, arms for personal use, livestock and poultry

levy.exempt.small_residence.value: any residence where the amount of the levy does not exceed $5,000

levy.exempt.tools.value: $5,990 of books and tools necessary for the taxpayer's trade, business or profession

levy.notice_days.value: no less than 30 days before the levy, given in person, left at the dwelling or usual place of business, or sent by certified or registered mail to the last known address

levy.redemption.value: 180 days after the sale, on payment of the purchase price plus interest at 20% per annum

lien.cdp_notice_days.value: within 5 business days after the notice of lien is filed, with the 30-day hearing window opening the day after that period

lien.refiling_period.value: the one-year period ending 30 days after the expiration of 10 years from the date of assessment, and each 10-year period after that

lien.release_days.value: not later than 30 days after the liability is satisfied or becomes legally unenforceable, or a bond is accepted

lke.basis.value: the basis of the property given up, decreased by money received and increased by gain or decreased by loss recognised — with a liability assumed by the other party, as determined under IRC § 357(d), treated as money received

lke.boot.value: gain is recognised to the extent of money and the fair market value of other property received, but not more than the realised gain — and a loss is never recognised on an exchange that would otherwise qualify

lke.exchange_period.value: the **earlier** of 180 days after the transfer of the relinquished property or the due date, including extensions, of the return for the year of that transfer — so a late-year sale needs an extension to get the full 180 days

lke.excluded_partnership.value: an interest in a partnership with a valid IRC § 761(a) election out of subchapter K is treated as an interest in each of its assets rather than as a partnership interest

lke.foreign.value: real property in the United States and real property outside it are not of like kind

lke.held_for_sale.value: unavailable for real property held primarily for sale — so a dealer's inventory and a developer's lots are outside the section

lke.identification_limits.value: three properties without regard to value; or any number whose aggregate value at the end of the identification period does not exceed 200 percent of the relinquished property's value; or, failing both, any identified property actually received amounting to at least 95 percent of the value of everything identified

lke.identification_period.value: 45 days after the transfer of the relinquished property, in an unambiguous written description — a legal description, street address or distinguishable name for real property

lke.related_party.value: nonrecognition is undone where, within 2 years of the last transfer in the exchange, the related person disposes of the property received or the taxpayer disposes of the property they received — the gain being taken into account in the year of that later disposition

lke.scope.value: real property only — no gain or loss on the exchange of real property held for productive use in a trade or business or for investment, solely for real property of like kind to be so held
lke.scope.source: IRC § 1031(a)(1), as amended by Pub. L. 115-97 § 13303(a) — https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/1031

llc.amount.value: 20 percent of up to $10,000 of qualified tuition and related expenses, a maximum of $2,000 per return rather than per student, entirely non-refundable

matherror.abatement_window.value: 60 days after the notice is sent, within which the taxpayer may request abatement and the Secretary must abate

medical.cosmetic.value: cosmetic surgery is not medical care unless necessary to ameliorate a deformity arising from or directly related to a congenital abnormality, a personal injury from accident or trauma, or a disfiguring disease

medical.decedent.value: expenses for the decedent's medical care paid out of the estate within the 1-year period beginning the day after death are treated as paid by the taxpayer when incurred — unless allowed as an IRC § 2053 estate tax deduction, which requires a waiver statement to avoid

medical.definition.value: amounts paid for diagnosis, cure, mitigation, treatment or prevention of disease or to affect any structure or function of the body; transportation primarily for and essential to that care; qualified long-term care services; and insurance covering such care

medical.drugs.value: an amount paid for medicine or a drug counts only if it is a prescribed drug or is insulin — so over-the-counter medicines are outside the deduction however medically necessary

medical.floor.value: 7.5 percent of adjusted gross income — a permanent figure since Pub. L. 116-260 § 101(a) struck the alternative, with no sunset in the text

medical.lodging.value: lodging away from home, not lavish or extravagant, primarily for and essential to medical care, counts where the care is provided by a physician in a licensed hospital or equivalent facility and there is no significant element of personal pleasure — capped at $50 per night per individual

medical.long_term_care_premiums.value: only eligible long-term care premiums within IRC § 213(d)(10) are taken into account for a qualified long-term care insurance contract, on the age-banded scale

medical.no_double_benefit.value: amounts allowed under the dependent care credit provisions are excluded, and an expense deducted elsewhere — including under IRC § 162(l) or paid from a health savings account — cannot be counted again here
medical.no_double_benefit.source: IRC § 213(e); § 162(l)(3); § 213(a) ("not compensated for by insurance or otherwise") — https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/213

medical.relatives.value: a payment for qualified long-term care services is treated as not paid for medical care where the service is provided by the individual's spouse or a relative unless they are a licensed professional, or by a related corporation or partnership

medical.whose_expenses.value: the taxpayer, spouse, or a dependent within IRC § 152 determined without regard to the gross income test, the not-a-dependent-of-another test, and the joint return test

misc.suspension.value: no miscellaneous itemized deduction is allowed for any taxable year beginning after 31 December 2017 — permanent since the 2026 end date was struck, and now at IRC § 67(h) rather than § 67(g)
misc.suspension.source: IRC § 67(h) as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70110(a), (b)(2) — https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/67

nii.tax.value: 3.8 percent of the lesser of net investment income or the excess of modified adjusted gross income over $250,000 on a joint return, $125,000 for a married individual filing separately, and $200,000 in any other case — none of the thresholds indexed

nqdc.409a_penalty.value: the deferred amount is included in gross income, and the tax for the year is increased by interest at the underpayment rate plus one percentage point from the year of deferral, plus 20 percent of the included compensation

nrded.charitable_domestic_only.value: the § 170 deduction reaches a corporation, trust, community chest, fund or foundation created or organised in the United States or a possession, so a gift to a foreign charity does not qualify even for a nonresident alien

nrded.effectively_connected.value: a nonresident alien engaged in a United States trade or business is taxed under IRC § 1 or § 55 on taxable income effectively connected with it, gross income including only effectively connected income

nrded.general_rule.value: deductions are allowed only for purposes of IRC § 871(b) and only if and to the extent connected with income effectively connected with a United States trade or business, apportioned and allocated as regulations provide

nrded.no_standard_deduction.value: zero — a nonresident alien individual is one of the four classes for which IRC § 63(c)(6) sets the standard deduction at zero, so itemising is not a choice

nrded.students_and_trainees.value: a nonresident alien temporarily present under an F, J, M or Q visa who is not otherwise engaged in a United States trade or business is treated as so engaged, and the income described in the second sentence of IRC § 1441(b) is treated as effectively connected to the extent from United States sources

nrded.three_exceptions.value: three deductions are allowed whether or not connected with effectively connected income — casualty and theft losses under IRC § 165(c)(2) or (3) but only for property located in the United States, charitable contributions under § 170, and the § 151 personal exemption limited to one unless the taxpayer is a resident of a contiguous country or a United States national

nua.aggregation.value: all trusts in a plan are one trust, all pension plans of the employer one plan, all profit-sharing plans one plan, and all stock bonus plans one plan — so the balance must be emptied across the whole category, not just the one account

nua.basis.value: the excluded appreciation is not included in the distributee's basis in the securities — basis is the trust's cost, which is the amount taxed as ordinary income in the year of distribution

nua.character.value: on a later sale the excluded appreciation is gain from the sale or exchange of a capital asset held long term, whatever the distributee's actual holding period; any further gain above it is long or short term on the distributee's own holding period

nua.definition.value: the excess of the market value of the securities at the time of distribution over their cost or other basis to the trust, taken net across appreciated and depreciated securities, with two distributions in one taxable year treated as one

nua.election_out.value: the exclusion applies automatically; the only election is an election not to have it apply, made on the return on which the lump sum distribution is required to be included

nua.eligible_plans.value: only a trust forming part of a § 401(a) plan and exempt under § 501, or a § 403(a) plan — no IRA of any kind can produce it, so a rollover of the securities to an IRA ends the opportunity permanently

nua.exclusion.value: on a lump sum distribution that includes employer securities, the net unrealized appreciation attributable to that part of the distribution is excluded from gross income

nua.lump_sum.value: the distribution within one taxable year of the recipient of the balance to the credit of the employee, payable on death, after age 59½, on separation from service, or after disability — from a § 401(a) exempt trust or a § 403(a) plan

nua.non_lump_sum.value: on a distribution that is not a lump sum, only the net unrealized appreciation attributable to amounts contributed by the employee is left out — and not at all where the distribution is rolled over under IRC § 402(c)

nua.securities.value: only shares of stock and bonds or debentures issued by a corporation with interest coupons or in registered form, including securities of a parent or subsidiary corporation as defined in IRC § 424(e) and (f)

offset.priority.value: internal revenue tax first, then past-due child support, then debts owed to federal agencies, then past-due state income tax, then covered unemployment compensation debts

offset.support_priority.value: past-due support certified by a State is applied first, before any other reduction allowed by law

oic.application_fee.source: IRS Offer in Compromise page and Form 656-B booklet

oic.lump_sum_initial.value: 20% of the total offer, with the application
oic.lump_sum_initial.source: IRS Offer in Compromise page and Form 656-B booklet; IRC § 7122(c)(1)(A)

oic.lump_sum_max_payments.source: IRS Offer in Compromise page and Form 656-B booklet; IRC § 7122(c)(1)(A)(ii)

options.disqualifying_disposition.value: where only the holding periods fail, the income increase and the employer's deduction fall in the year of the **disposition** rather than the year of exercise — and no chapter 24 withholding is required on it

options.espp_discount_compensation.value: where the option price was below full value at grant, a qualifying disposition or death still produces compensation — the lesser of the excess of value at disposition over the price paid, or the excess of value at grant over the option price — added to basis and not subject to withholding

options.espp_holding.value: no disposition within 2 years after the grant nor within 1 year after the share is transferred, and employment at all times from grant until 3 months before exercise

options.espp_price_and_limits.value: an option price of not less than 85 percent of value at grant or at exercise; an option period of 5 years where the price is set against value at exercise; and no employee accruing rights to purchase more than $25,000 of stock, valued at grant, for each calendar year the option is outstanding

options.grantor_character.value: for the grantor of an option in stock, securities or commodities, gain or loss on a closing transaction and gain on lapse are short-term capital — treated as from the sale of a capital asset held not more than 1 year

options.iso_amt.value: IRC § 421 does not apply for alternative minimum tax purposes, so the bargain element at exercise is an adjustment and the AMT basis of the stock differs from its regular tax basis

options.iso_annual_limit.value: options first exercisable in a calendar year, across all plans of the employer and its parents and subsidiaries, for stock whose aggregate value at grant exceeds $100,000 are not incentive stock options — applied in the order the options were granted

options.iso_holding.value: no disposition within 2 years from the grant nor within 1 year after the share is transferred, and employment with the granting corporation or a parent or subsidiary at all times from grant until 3 months before exercise

options.iso_plan_terms.value: a shareholder-approved plan; grant within 10 years of adoption or approval; not exercisable more than 10 years after grant; an option price not less than fair market value at grant; non-transferable except by will or descent; and the holder owning not more than 10 percent of the voting power at grant

options.purchaser_character.value: gain or loss on the sale of an option, or loss from failing to exercise it, has the same character as the underlying property would have in the taxpayer's hands — and an option that lapses is deemed sold on the day it expired

options.reporting.value: a corporation transferring stock on the exercise of an incentive stock option, or recording a transfer of title to stock acquired under an IRC § 423(c) option, must file a return and furnish a statement to the individual

options.statutory_effect.value: on a qualifying transfer no income results at exercise, the employer gets no IRC § 162 deduction, and nothing beyond the option price is treated as received by the corporation for the share

otheritem.claim_of_right.value: where an item was included in a prior year because it appeared the taxpayer had an unrestricted right to it, and a deduction of more than $3,000 becomes allowable because that proved wrong, tax is the lesser of the tax computed with the deduction or the tax computed without it less the decrease in prior-year tax

otheritem.gambling_losses.value: allowed as an itemized deduction outside the miscellaneous class, but only within the IRC § 165(d) ceiling as rewritten by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70114(a)

otheritem.impairment_related.value: expenses of a handicapped individual for attendant care at the place of employment and other expenses necessary to enable them to work, deductible in full without a floor

otheritem.ird_estate_tax.value: a deduction for the federal estate tax attributable to an item of income in respect of a decedent, allowed to whoever includes that income and computed as a ratio of the estate tax to the net value of all such items

otheritem.miscellaneous_gone.value: everything not on the § 67(b) list is a miscellaneous itemized deduction and is allowed **nowhere** — permanently, since Pub. L. 119-21 § 70110 struck the end date and redesignated the subsection as § 67(h)

otheritem.survivors.value: thirteen classes are carved out of the definition of a miscellaneous itemized deduction and therefore survive the IRC § 67(h) disallowance — interest, taxes, casualty and theft and wagering losses, charitable contributions, medical expenses, impairment-related work expenses, the § 691(c) estate tax deduction, short sale expenses, § 1341 claim of right, § 72(b)(3) unrecovered annuity investment, amortizable bond premium, cooperative housing, and educator expenses

overtime.deduction_cap.value: $12,500 of qualified overtime compensation, or $25,000 on a joint return, reduced by $100 for each $1,000 of modified adjusted gross income above $150,000, or $300,000 joint
overtime.deduction_cap.source: IRC § 225(b)(1), (b)(2)(A) as added by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70202(a) — https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/225

passive.active_participation.value: a 10 percent interest by value in the activity, counting a spouse's interest, is the minimum — a lower threshold than material participation but not nothing

passive.material_participation_tests.value: seven, any one of which suffices — more than 500 hours; substantially all the participation of anyone; more than 100 hours and no less than anyone else's; significant participation activities aggregating over 500 hours; material participation in five of the ten preceding years; a personal service activity with material participation in any three preceding years; or regular, continuous and substantial participation on all the facts

passive.real_estate_professional.value: more than one-half of all personal services in trades or businesses performed in real property trades or businesses in which the taxpayer materially participates, and more than 750 hours of such services — on a joint return either spouse must satisfy both separately

passive.rental_offset.value: $25,000 of loss from rental real estate in which the individual actively participated, reduced by 50 cents for each dollar of adjusted gross income above $100,000 and so gone at $150,000 — neither figure indexed since 1986

passport.reversal_timing.value: within 30 days of an installment agreement being entered into, an offer being accepted, or an innocent spouse election or request; and by the § 6325(a) lien release deadline where the debt is satisfied or becomes unenforceable

passport.state_hold.value: 90 days from the date of the State Department's letter to arrange payment, pay in full, or resolve an erroneous certification
passport.state_hold.source: irs.gov, Revocation or denial of passport in cases of certain unpaid taxes, opened 2026-08-18

passport.threshold.value: more than $66,000 of assessed, unpaid, legally enforceable federal tax liability including penalties and interest
passport.threshold.source: IRC § 7345(b)(1)(B), indexed under § 7345(f); Rev. Proc. 2025-32; irs.gov passport page opened 2026-08-18

passthrough.loss_basis_limit.value: a partner's distributive share of loss only to the extent of the adjusted basis of the partnership interest at the end of that partnership year; an S corporation shareholder's losses only to the sum of stock basis and the basis of any debt the corporation owes them

penalty.accuracy.gross_valuation.value: 40% of the underpayment attributable to a gross valuation misstatement

penalty.fraud.rate.value: 75% of the underpayment attributable to fraud

penalty.frivolous.value: $5,000 per frivolous return or specified frivolous submission

penalty.ftf.minimum.value: the lesser of $535 or 100% of the tax required to be shown, for returns required to be filed in 2027
penalty.ftf.minimum.source: IRC § 6651(a) flush language and § 6651(j); Rev. Proc. 2025-32 § 3.52

penalty.ftf.rate.value: 5% of the tax per month or part month, maximum 25%

penalty.ftp.rate.value: 0.5% of the tax per month or part month, maximum 25%

penalty.substantial_understatement.thres.value: an understatement exceeding the greater of 10% of the tax required to be shown or $5,000 (corporations: the lesser of the greater of 10% or $10,000, or $10,000,000)

penalty.valuation.thresholds.value: substantial at 150% or more of the correct value or adjusted basis; gross at 200% or more

personalrental.se_exclusion.value: self-employment income excludes rentals from real estate and from personal property leased *with* the real estate — personal property let on its own is not excluded

plan.mandatory_withholding.value: 20 percent of an eligible rollover distribution, unless the distributee elects a direct trustee-to-trustee payment under IRC § 401(a)(31)(A)

plan.not_eligible_rollover.value: substantially equal periodic payments over a life, joint lives or a period of 10 years or more; any amount required under IRC § 401(a)(9); and any hardship distribution

plan.rollover_window.value: 60 days following the day the distributee received the property, with a hardship waiver where enforcing it would be against equity or good conscience

plan.simplified_method.value: the investment in the contract at the annuity starting date divided by the number of anticipated payments from the statutory table — 360 payments where the annuitant is 55 or under, falling in bands as the starting age rises

planloan.aggregation.value: all loans from the plan are added together, and all plans of an employer — determined after applying the controlled group, common control and affiliated service group rules of IRC § 414(b), (c) and (m) — are treated as one plan

planloan.amortization.value: substantially level amortization over the term of the loan, with payments not less frequently than quarterly — suspended for up to one year of a bona fide unpaid leave of absence, but the latest permissible term is not extended

planloan.credit_card.value: no exception at all — a loan made through a credit card or any similar arrangement is a distribution in full, regardless of amount or terms

planloan.cure_period.value: a plan administrator may allow a cure period for a missed installment, but it cannot run beyond the last day of the calendar quarter following the quarter in which the payment was due

planloan.deemed_distribution.value: taxed under IRC § 72 as if it were an actual distribution, including the additional tax under § 72(t) — but it is not an actual distribution, so it is not eligible for rollover and does not reduce the account balance

planloan.disaster_increase.value: for a qualified individual borrowing during the applicable period for a qualified disaster, $100,000 replaces $50,000 and the whole nonforfeitable accrued benefit replaces one-half of it, with repayments due in the relief period delayed a year

planloan.exemption_conditions.value: available to all participants and beneficiaries on a reasonably equivalent basis, not more generous to highly compensated employees, made under specific plan provisions, bearing a reasonable rate of interest and adequately secured

planloan.interest_deduction.value: denied for a key employee as defined in IRC § 416(i), and denied to anyone where the loan is secured by amounts attributable to elective deferrals

planloan.ira.value: no loan is possible — a qualified employer plan for this purpose is a § 401(a), § 403(a) or § 403(b) plan, and lending between an IRA and its owner is a prohibited transaction whose consequence is loss of the account's status

planloan.limit.value: the lesser of $50,000 reduced by the excess of the highest outstanding loan balance during the 1-year period ending the day before the loan over the balance on the day of the loan, or the greater of one-half the present value of the nonforfeitable accrued benefit or $10,000

planloan.offset_rollover.value: a qualified plan loan offset amount — one arising solely from plan termination or from severance from employment — may be rolled over as late as the due date, including extensions, for the return for the year of the deemed distribution

planloan.term.value: the loan must by its terms be repayable within 5 years, unless it is used to acquire a dwelling unit that within a reasonable time is to be the participant's principal residence — a test applied when the loan is made

plr.definition.value: a written statement issued to a taxpayer or their authorized representative by the National Office, which interprets and applies the tax laws to a specific set of facts; rulings are issued only by the National Office

plr.determination_letter.value: a written statement issued in response to a written inquiry, applying to the particular facts the principles and precedents previously announced by the National Office — issued only where the determination can be made on clearly established rules in a statute, Treasury decision, regulation, or a ruling, opinion or court decision published in the Internal Revenue Bulletin, and not where the question is novel

plr.information_letter.value: a statement that does no more than call attention to a well-established interpretation or principle of tax law, without applying it to a specific set of facts — issued where the request seeks general information or does not meet all the requirements for a ruling

plr.user_fees.value: user fees are required for requests for ruling letters, opinion letters and determination letters; they vary by category, are set after taking account of the average time for and difficulty of the category, and are payable in advance — with exemptions and reduced fees as the Secretary determines appropriate

poa.agent_signature_grounds.value: disease or injury; continuous absence from the United States, including Puerto Rico, for at least 60 days before the due date of the return; or specific permission requested of and granted by the IRS for other good cause
poa.agent_signature_grounds.source: Reg. § 1.6012-1(a)(5), quoted in the Instructions for Form 2848 (rev. 09/2021), line 5a — https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/26/1.6012-1

poa.notice_copy_limit.value: no more than 2 representatives on a Form 2848 — or designees on a Form 8821 — may be designated to receive copies of notices and communications for the same matters
poa.notice_copy_limit.source: Instructions for Form 2848 (rev. 09/2021), line 2, page last reviewed 30 April 2026 — https://www.irs.gov/instructions/i2848

practice.irs_scope.value: all matters connected with a presentation to the IRS or any of its officers or employees relating to a taxpayer's rights, privileges or liabilities — including preparing and filing documents, corresponding and communicating with the IRS, rendering written advice on any entity, transaction, plan or arrangement having a potential for tax avoidance or evasion, and representing a client at conferences, hearings and meetings

preparer.6060.retention.value: 3 years following the close of the return period to which the record relates

preparer.6060.return_period.value: the 12-month period beginning on 1 July each year

preparer.6694a.value: the greater of $1,000 or 50% of the income derived or to be derived from the return or claim

preparer.6694a.assessment_period.value: 3 years from the filing of the return or claim

preparer.6694b.value: the greater of $5,000 or 75% of the income derived or to be derived from the return or claim

preparer.6694b.assessment_period.value: no limitation period — assessable at any time

preparer.6695.per_failure.value: $65 per return or claim, capped at $33,000
preparer.6695.per_failure.source: Rev. Proc. 2025-32 § 3.54 (returns or claims filed in 2027); IRC § 6695(a)–(e)

preparer.6695B.assessment_period.value: 6 years from the filing of the return or claim

preparer.6695f.check.source: Rev. Proc. 2025-32 § 3.54 (returns or claims filed in 2027); IRC § 6695(f)

preparer.6695g.duediligence.source: Rev. Proc. 2025-32 § 3.54 (returns or claims filed in 2027); IRC § 6695(g)

preparer.6701.corporate.value: $10,000 per document where the document relates to a corporation's tax liability

preparer.6701.individual.value: $1,000 per document, and only one penalty per person per taxpayer per taxable period

preparer.6713.assessment_period.value: no limitation period — § 6696(d) does not reach § 6713

preparer.6713.per_disclosure.value: $250 per disclosure or use, capped at $10,000 per calendar year

preparer.7216.criminal.value: a misdemeanor: a fine of up to $1,000, imprisonment of up to one year, or both, plus costs of prosecution

preparer.consent_windows.value: a consent is sought when under 180 days remain, and must be obtained if the case goes to Appeals with under 365 days remaining

preparer.office_practice_elements.value: a system for promoting accuracy and consistency that, for a signing preparer, generally includes checklists, methods for obtaining necessary information from the taxpayer, a review of the prior year's return, and review procedures
preparer.office_practice_elements.source: Reg. § 1.6694-2(e), Exception for reasonable cause and good faith — https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/26/1.6694-2

preparer.reasonable_cause_factors.value: 6 — the nature of the error causing the understatement, the frequency of errors, the materiality of errors, the preparer's normal office practice, reliance on the advice of others, and reliance on generally accepted administrative or industry practice
preparer.reasonable_cause_factors.source: Reg. § 1.6694-2(e), Exception for reasonable cause and good faith — https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/26/1.6694-2

preparer.records_retention_6107.value: 3 years after the close of the return period — a completed copy, or a list of taxpayer names and identifying numbers

preparer.refund_claim_period.value: 3 years from the date the penalty was paid

preparer.stay_of_collection.value: 15% of the penalty, paid within 30 days of notice and demand, with a refund claim

preparer.suit_window.value: 30 days after the earlier of denial of the refund claim or the expiration of 6 months from filing it

privilege.7525_forums.value: any noncriminal tax matter before the IRS, and any noncriminal tax proceeding in Federal court brought by or against the United States

privilege.7525_shelter_exception.value: no privilege for any written communication between a federally authorized tax practitioner and any person (or that person's director, officer, employee, agent, representative, or capital- or profits-interest holder) in connection with the promotion of that person's direct or indirect participation in a tax shelter

privilege.tax_shelter_definition.value: a partnership or other entity, any investment plan or arrangement, or any other plan or arrangement, if a significant purpose of it is the avoidance or evasion of Federal income tax

prizes.charity_transfer.value: three conditions, all required — the recipient was selected without any action to enter, is not required to render substantial future services, and the payor transfers the award to a governmental unit or IRC § 170(c)(1) or (2) organisation on the recipient's designation

prohibited.categories.value: six, each reaching any direct **or indirect** dealing — sale, exchange or lease of property; lending or extension of credit; furnishing of goods, services or facilities; transfer to or use by or for the benefit of a disqualified person of plan income or assets; a fiduciary dealing with plan income or assets in his own interest; and a fiduciary receiving consideration for his own account from a party dealing with the plan

prohibited.disqualified_person.value: a fiduciary; a service provider to the plan; an employer or employee organization whose people are covered; a 50 percent owner of such an employer or organization; a member of the family of most of those; an entity 50 percent owned by them; and officers, directors and highly compensated employees

prohibited.excise_tax.value: 15 percent of the amount involved for each year or part of a year in the taxable period, and a further 100 percent of the amount involved if the transaction is not corrected within that period — both paid by the disqualified person who participated

prohibited.ira_consequence.value: the account ceases to be an individual retirement account as of the **first day** of the taxable year, and is treated as distributing all its assets at their fair market value on that day — with the owner and beneficiaries then exempt from the IRC § 4975 excise taxes

prohibited.pledge.value: using an individual retirement account or any portion of it as security for a loan treats the portion so used as distributed — a partial consequence, not the total disqualification that a prohibited transaction brings

ptin.fee.value: $18.75 to apply or renew — a $10 annual IRS fee plus $8.75 charged by the contractor
ptin.fee.source: Reg. § 300.11 (applies from 30 September 2025); irs.gov PTIN requirements page

ptp.751_ordinary.value: so much of the amount received as is attributable to unrealized receivables or inventory items is treated as realized from the sale of property **other than** a capital asset — ordinary income, whatever the holding period

ptp.corporate_default.value: treated as a corporation for purposes of the whole title, except where the passive-type income exception applies

ptp.definition.value: a partnership whose interests are traded on an established securities market, or are readily tradable on a secondary market or the substantial equivalent — the same two-limb test appears in IRC § 7704(b) and § 469(k)(2)
