hctc.expiry.value: expired — IRC § 35(b)(1)(B) requires an eligible coverage month to begin before 1 January 2022, so no health coverage tax credit has been available since taxable year 2021

amt.exemption.value: $140,200 on a joint return or for a surviving spouse, $90,100 for an unmarried individual, $70,100 for a married individual filing separately and $31,400 for an estate or trust, for taxable years beginning in 2026

amt.phase_out.value: the exemption is reduced by 50 cents for each dollar of alternative minimum taxable income above $1,000,000 on a joint return and $500,000 in every other individual case, disappearing at $1,280,400 joint, $680,200 unmarried, $640,200 married filing separately and $167,600 for an estate or trust (2026)

amt.phase_out_rate.value: 50 percent for taxable years beginning after 31 December 2025, doubled from 25 percent by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70107(c), which added IRC § 55(d)(4)(A)(ii)(IV)
amt.phase_out_rate.source: IRC § 55 as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70107, read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/55

amt.rates.value: 26 percent of the taxable excess up to $244,500, and 28 percent above it — half that breakpoint, $122,250, for a married individual filing separately (2026)

amt.permanence.value: permanent — Pub. L. 119-21 § 70107(a) struck the words limiting IRC § 55(d)(4) to taxable years beginning before 2026 from both the heading and the text, for taxable years beginning after 31 December 2025
amt.permanence.source: IRC § 55 as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70107, read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/55

amt.threshold_reset.value: the phase-out threshold was reset to $1,000,000 joint and $500,000 otherwise and re-indexed from calendar year 2025 rather than 2017, so the 2026 figure is materially lower than the 2025 one (IRC § 55(d)(4)(B)(i), (i)(II)(2))
amt.threshold_reset.source: IRC § 55 as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70107, read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/55

amt.credit.value: the minimum tax credit carries forward without limit, and in any year is capped at regular tax liability reduced by other nonrefundable credits, less the tentative minimum tax for that year — and only deferral items generate it, never exclusion items (IRC § 53(b), (c), (d)(1)(B))

household.fica_rate.value: 6.2 percent for social security and 1.45 percent for Medicare withheld from the employee, matched by the same 7.65 percent from the employer
household.fica_rate.source: IRS Topic no. 756, Employment taxes for household employees, read at irs.gov/taxtopics/tc756

household.excluded_workers.value: a spouse, a child under 21, a parent unless an exception is met, and an employee under 18 at any time in the year unless household work is that employee's principal occupation — a student's household work is never their principal occupation
household.excluded_workers.source: IRS Topic no. 756, Employment taxes for household employees, read at irs.gov/taxtopics/tc756

household.income_tax_withholding.value: not required — an employer withholds federal income tax from a household employee only if both agree to it, though social security and Medicare withholding is mandatory once the threshold is met
household.income_tax_withholding.source: IRS Topic no. 756, Employment taxes for household employees, read at irs.gov/taxtopics/tc756

household.threshold_mechanism.value: a $1,000 statutory base adjusted each year by the Commissioner of Social Security under the average wage index in section 215(a)(1)(B)(ii) of the Social Security Act with 1993 as the base year, rounded down to the next lowest multiple of $100 — so it can stand still for a year while the index rises

estpen.required_annual_payment.value: the lesser of 90 percent of the tax shown on this year's return or 100 percent of the tax shown on last year's — raised to 110 percent where last year's adjusted gross income exceeded $150,000, or $75,000 for a married individual filing separately (IRC § 6654(d)(1)(B), (C))

estpen.installments.value: four, due 15 April, 15 June, 15 September and 15 January of the following year, each 25 percent of the required annual payment (IRC § 6654(c)(1), (2), (d)(1)(A))

estpen.de_minimis.value: no addition to tax where the tax shown on the return, reduced by the IRC § 31 credit for tax withheld, is less than $1,000 (IRC § 6654(e)(1))

estpen.no_prior_liability.value: no addition to tax where the preceding taxable year was a full 12 months, the individual had no tax liability for it, and the individual was a citizen or resident throughout it (IRC § 6654(e)(2))

estpen.retirement_waiver.value: discretionary, not automatic — the Secretary must determine both that the taxpayer retired after attaining age 62 or became disabled, in the year estimated payments were due or the year before, and that the underpayment was due to reasonable cause and not willful neglect (IRC § 6654(e)(3)(B))

interest.underpayment_rate.value: the federal short-term rate plus 3 percentage points, redetermined quarterly (IRC § 6621(a)(2)) — for 2026 the IRS has published 7 percent for the first quarter, 6 percent for the second and 7 percent for the third; the fourth-quarter rate is not yet published
interest.underpayment_rate.source: IRS Quarterly interest rates, read at irs.gov/payments/quarterly-interest-rates

interest.overpayment_rate.value: the federal short-term rate plus 3 percentage points for a non-corporate taxpayer, 2 points for a corporation (IRC § 6621(a)(1)) — 7 percent for the first and third quarters of 2026 and 6 percent for the second
interest.overpayment_rate.source: IRS Quarterly interest rates, read at irs.gov/payments/quarterly-interest-rates

ftf_ftp.rates.value: failure to file, 5 percent of the net tax due for each month or part month, capped at 25 percent; failure to pay, 0.5 percent a month on the same cap, reduced to 0.25 percent while an installment agreement is in effect for a return filed on time and raised to 1 percent from ten days after a notice of intent to levy (IRC § 6651(a)(1), (2), (d), (h))

ftf.minimum.value: for a return required to be filed in 2027 and filed more than 60 days late, the failure to file addition is not less than the lesser of $535 or 100 percent of the tax required to be shown — the § 6651(a) figure of $435 as indexed
ftf.minimum.source: IRC § 6651(a) read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/6651 and Rev. Proc. 2025-32 § 3.52 read at irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/rp-25-32.pdf

ftf_ftp.interaction.value: for any month in which both apply, the failure to file addition is reduced by the failure to pay addition — but never below the 60-day minimum (IRC § 6651(c)(1))

estpen.unindexed.value: none of the § 6654 figures is indexed — the $1,000 de minimis, the $150,000 and $75,000 prior-year income thresholds and the 90, 100 and 110 percent tests are all statutory and unchanged, the income thresholds since 1993

se.optional_limits.value: set by IRC § 1402(l): the lower limit for a year is the sum of the amounts required under section 213(d) of the Social Security Act for a quarter of coverage for each calendar quarter in the year, and the upper limit is 150 percent of that — so both move with an SSA figure rather than with a Treasury inflation adjustment

se.optional_2025.value: the most recently published Schedule SE figures are for 2025: the farm optional method is available where gross farm income was $10,860 or less or net farm profits were under $7,840, and reports two thirds of gross farm income up to $7,240 — the 2026 instructions have not been issued, so no 2026 figure is stated here
se.optional_2025.source: Instructions for Schedule SE (Form 1040) (2025), page last reviewed 30 April 2026, read at irs.gov/instructions/i1040sse

se.optional_farm.value: two thirds of gross farm income where that income does not exceed the upper limit, or the lower limit where gross farm income exceeds the upper limit but net earnings fall below the lower limit — available for an unlimited number of years (IRC § 1402(a), clauses (i) and (ii) of the agricultural sentence)

se.optional_nonfarm.value: the same two thirds computation for a non-farm trade or business, but only for a taxpayer self-employed on a regular basis within IRC § 1402(h) — net earnings of at least $400 in two of the three preceding years — and for no more than five taxable years in a lifetime

se.minister_exemption.value: an irrevocable exemption available to a duly ordained, commissioned or licensed minister, a member of a religious order who has not taken a vow of poverty, or a Christian Science practitioner, on an application stating conscientious or religious opposition to public insurance for death, disability, old age, retirement or medical care (IRC § 1402(e)(1))

se.religious_sect_exemption.value: available to a member and adherent of a recognised religious sect conscientiously opposed to public or private insurance benefits, on an application supported by evidence of membership and of the sect's established tenets (IRC § 1402(g)(1))

excess_ss.maximum.value: 6.2 percent of the 2026 contribution and benefit base of $184,500 — $11,439.00 of old-age, survivors and disability insurance tax per employer, the ceiling above which a multi-employer taxpayer has an excess
excess_ss.maximum.source: IRS Topic no. 751 (page last reviewed 20 January 2026), read at irs.gov/taxtopics/tc751

excess_ss.two_employer_test.value: the credit arises only where the employee received wages from more than one employer during the calendar year and the combined wages exceed the contribution and benefit base — a single employer that over-withholds must refund the employee and issue a corrected Form W-2 (IRC § 6413(c)(1))
excess_ss.two_employer_test.source: IRC §§ 31(b) and 6413(c), read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/31 and /6413

excess_ss.character.value: treated as an amount withheld at source as tax under IRC § 3402, so it is a payment rather than a subpart A credit — it is refundable, it is not limited by tax liability, and it reduces no particular tax (IRC § 31(b)(1))
excess_ss.character.source: IRC §§ 31(b) and 6413(c), read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/31 and /6413

excess_ss.year.value: allowed as a credit for the taxable year beginning in the calendar year in which the wages were received, so a fiscal-year taxpayer takes it against the year that began in the calendar year of the wages (IRC § 31(b)(2))
excess_ss.year.source: IRC §§ 31(b) and 6413(c), read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/31 and /6413

excess_ss.medicare.value: none — the hospital insurance tax under IRC § 3101(b)(1) has no wage ceiling, and the 0.9 percent additional Medicare tax under § 3101(b)(2) is reconciled on the taxpayer's own return rather than through this credit

excess_ss.rrta.value: railroad retirement tier 1 tax under IRC § 3201(a) counts toward the same ceiling, but only to the extent of the rate that does not exceed the § 3101(a) rate, and § 3231(e) compensation is treated as wages for this purpose (IRC § 6413(c)(1))
excess_ss.rrta.source: IRC §§ 31(b) and 6413(c), read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/31 and /6413

clergy.housing_exclusion.value: the rental value of a home furnished as part of compensation is excluded outright; a cash rental allowance is excluded only to the extent used to rent or provide a home and only up to the fair rental value of the home with furnishings and appurtenances plus utilities (IRC § 107(1), (2))

clergy.designation.value: a cash allowance must be designated as a rental allowance by official action of the employing church taken in advance of the payment — an employment contract, minutes, a resolution or the budget will do, but a designation made after the fact will not (Reg. § 1.107-1(b))

clergy.se_inclusion.value: net earnings from ministerial service are computed without regard to IRC §§ 107, 119 and 911, so the excluded housing value or allowance is nonetheless subject to self-employment tax (IRC § 1402(a)(8))

clergy.retirement_carve_out.value: the rental value of a parsonage or a parsonage allowance provided after retirement, and any other retirement benefit from a church plan within IRC § 414(e), are excluded from net earnings from self-employment (IRC § 1402(a)(8))

clergy.exemptions.value: two, and only two — a member of a religious order who has taken a vow of poverty is outside self-employment tax without applying, and any other minister or Christian Science practitioner must file and have approved an application stating conscientious or religious opposition to public insurance (IRC § 1402(c) closing sentence, § 1402(e)(1))

clergy.withholding.value: ministerial services are excluded from wages for income tax withholding and from employment for FICA, so a minister pays through estimated tax or a voluntary withholding agreement (IRC §§ 3401(a)(9) and 3121(b)(8)(A))
clergy.withholding.source: IRC §§ 3401(a)(9) and 3121(b)(8)(A), read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/3401 and /3121

clergy.double_deduction.value: mortgage interest and real property taxes on the minister's home remain deductible even though paid out of an excluded parsonage allowance — IRC § 265(a)(6)(B) disapplies the usual denial of deductions allocable to tax-exempt income

military.combat_exclusion.value: unlimited for an enlisted member or a warrant officer, and capped for a commissioned officer at the maximum enlisted amount — the highest basic pay payable to an enlisted member at the highest pay grade for that month, plus any hostile fire or imminent danger pay the officer receives (IRC § 112(a), (b), (c)(1), (5))

military.month_rule.value: service in a combat zone for any part of a month excludes that whole month's compensation, and the exclusion extends to a month of hospitalisation from wounds, disease or injury incurred there — but not to a month beginning more than two years after combatant activities in the zone terminate (IRC § 112(a), (b))

military.not_compensation.value: pensions and retirement pay are outside the exclusion however the recipient served (IRC § 112(c)(4))

military.combat_zone_designation.value: a combat zone exists only where the President designates one by Executive order, and service counts only between the Executive-order dates for the commencement and termination of combatant activities (IRC § 112(c)(2), (3))

military.deadline_suspension.value: the period of service in a combat zone or a designated contingency operation, plus any continuous qualified hospitalisation for an injury received there, plus 180 days, is disregarded for filing, payment, assessment, collection, refund claims and Tax Court petitions alike (IRC § 7508(a))

military.death_forgiveness.value: no income tax applies for the year of death, or for any earlier year ending on or after the first day of combat zone service, where a member dies in active service in a combat zone or from wounds, disease or injury incurred there — and tax already assessed for earlier years is abated (IRC § 692(a))

military.moving_expenses.value: the § 217 deduction survives only for a member of the Armed Forces on active duty moving under military orders incident to a permanent change of station — the § 217(c) distance and time limits are switched off and in-kind moves or allowances are excluded from income — and from 2026 the same treatment extends to a member of the intelligence community relocating on assignment (IRC § 217(g), (k))
military.moving_expenses.source: IRC § 217(g), (k) as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70113, read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/217

military.residence_suspension.value: a taxpayer on qualified official extended duty may elect to suspend the running of the § 121 five-year period, for up to ten years, so a long deployment does not cost the exclusion on the sale of a principal residence (IRC § 121(d)(9)(A), (B))

military.reservist_travel.value: travel expenses of a member of a reserve component are deductible above the line, at rates not exceeding the federal per diem and travel rates, for any period the member is more than 100 miles from home (IRC § 62(a)(2)(E))

military.qualified_benefits.value: an allowance or in-kind benefit received by reason of service, other than personal use of a vehicle, that was excludable on 9 September 1986 under a law, regulation or administrative practice outside the Code — the housing and subsistence allowances rest on this rather than on any current statute (IRC § 134(a), (b)(1))

ird.definition.value: items of gross income of the decedent not properly includible in the taxable period in which the date of death falls or an earlier period — taxed to the estate if the right passes to it, to whoever acquires the right by reason of the death, or to the legatee if the estate has already distributed the right (IRC § 691(a)(1)(A)–(C))

ird.character.value: unchanged — the right is treated in the recipient's hands as if acquired in the transaction in which the right to the income was originally derived, so ordinary stays ordinary and capital gain stays capital gain with the decedent's holding period (IRC § 691(a)(3))

ird.no_basis_step_up.value: none — IRC § 1014(c) disapplies the date-of-death basis rule to property constituting a right to receive an item of income in respect of a decedent, which is why the item is taxed at all

ird.transfer.value: transferring the right accelerates the income: the transferor includes the fair market value of the right at the time of transfer, plus any consideration above that value — but transmission at death to the estate, or to a person entitled by reason of the death or by bequest, is not a transfer (IRC § 691(a)(2))

ird.deductions.value: deductions under IRC §§ 162, 163, 164, 212 and 611 and the § 27 foreign tax credit that were not allowable to the decedent are allowed when paid — to the estate, or to whoever takes the property subject to the obligation where the estate is not liable; depletion follows the income instead (IRC § 691(b)(1), (2))

ird.estate_tax_deduction.value: a deduction for the federal estate tax attributable to the item, computed as the ratio the value of the item bears to the net value of all such items, applied to the estate tax attributable to that net value — an itemized deduction, but expressly outside the definition of a miscellaneous itemized deduction, so it survives the § 67(h) disallowance (IRC § 691(c)(1), (2); § 67(b)(7))
ird.estate_tax_deduction.source: IRC §§ 691(c) and 67(b)(7), read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/691 and /67

niit.rate.value: 3.8 percent of the lesser of net investment income or the excess of modified adjusted gross income over the threshold — so the tax is never on more than the investment income and never on more than the amount above the threshold (IRC § 1411(a)(1))

niit.threshold.value: $250,000 on a joint return or for a surviving spouse, $125,000 for a married individual filing separately, and $200,000 in any other case — statutory, and never indexed since the tax took effect in 2013 (IRC § 1411(b))

niit.estate_threshold.value: for an estate or trust, 3.8 percent of the lesser of undistributed net investment income or the excess of adjusted gross income over the dollar amount at which the highest § 1(e) bracket begins — $16,250 for taxable years beginning in 2026
niit.estate_threshold.source: IRC § 1411(a)(2) read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/1411 and Rev. Proc. 2025-32 § 3.01 Table 5 read at irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/rp-25-32.pdf

niit.components.value: gross income from interest, dividends, annuities, royalties and rents unless derived in the ordinary course of a non-passive trade or business; other gross income from a passive activity or a trade or business of trading in financial instruments or commodities; and net gain from disposing of property other than property held in a non-passive trade or business — less the deductions properly allocable to them (IRC § 1411(c)(1), (2))

niit.exclusions.value: distributions from a plan or arrangement described in IRC §§ 401(a), 403(a), 403(b), 408, 408A or 457(b), and any item taken into account in determining self-employment income on which the § 1401(b) tax is imposed — so the same dollar is never hit by both the net investment income tax and the Medicare tax (IRC § 1411(c)(5), (6))

niit.nonapplication.value: a nonresident alien is outside the tax entirely, as is a trust all of whose unexpired interests are devoted to § 170(c)(2)(B) purposes (IRC § 1411(e))

niit.magi.value: adjusted gross income increased by the excess of the amount excluded under IRC § 911(a)(1) over the deductions and exclusions disallowed by reason of that exclusion (IRC § 1411(d))

addmed.rate.value: 0.9 percent of wages, and of self-employment income, above the threshold — imposed on the employee alone, with no employer match (IRC §§ 3101(b)(2) and 1401(b)(2))
addmed.rate.source: IRC §§ 3101(b)(2) and 1401(b)(2), read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/3101 and /1401

addmed.threshold.value: $250,000 on a joint return, $125,000 for a married individual filing separately and $200,000 in any other case — the same figures as the net investment income tax, equally unindexed (IRC § 3101(b)(2)(A)–(C))

addmed.withholding.value: an employer withholds only on wages it pays above $200,000, disregarding the spouse's wages and any other employer's — so withholding routinely fails to match the liability in both directions, and the difference is settled on Form 8959 (IRC § 3102(f)(1), (2))

uncollected.tip_reporting.value: an employee who receives tips constituting wages in any calendar month must report them to the employer in a written statement by the tenth day of the following month (IRC § 6053(a))

uncollected.collection_limit.value: the employer collects the employee's FICA on reported tips only from wages other than tips that are under its control, and only up to the tenth day of the month after the tips were deemed paid — anything it cannot reach is uncollected (IRC § 3102(c)(1))

uncollected.employer_statement.value: where the tax on reported tips exceeds what the employer can collect, the employer must furnish the employee a written statement showing the excess (IRC § 6053(b)) — it reaches the employee as codes A and B in box 12 of the Form W-2

uncollected.unreported_tips.value: tips of $20 or more in a month that the employee never reported to the employer are still wages, and the employee owes the social security and Medicare tax on them directly, computed on Form 4137

uncollected.tip_penalty.value: 50 percent of the tax on tips the employee failed to report as § 6053(a) required, unless the failure was due to reasonable cause and not wilful neglect (IRC § 6652(b))

uncollected.group_term_life.value: the cost of employer-provided group-term life insurance above $50,000 of coverage is included in the employee's gross income, and where the covered person is a former employee the employer cannot withhold on it — the tax appears as codes M and N in box 12 and is paid by the individual

other_taxes.fthb_recapture.value: 6⅔ percent of the credit for each taxable year of the 15-year recapture period, which begins with the second taxable year after the year of purchase — so a $7,500 credit repays at $500 a year (IRC § 36(f)(1), (7))

other_taxes.fthb_acceleration.value: disposing of the residence, or its ceasing to be the principal residence, before the end of the recapture period accelerates the whole unrecaptured balance into that year — capped, on a sale to an unrelated person, at the gain on the sale (IRC § 36(f)(2), (3))

other_taxes.fthb_exceptions.value: no recapture for any taxable year ending after the taxpayer's death; no acceleration on an involuntary conversion where a new principal residence is acquired within two years, the new residence taking the old one's place; and no acceleration on a § 1041(a) transfer between spouses or incident to divorce, the transferee taking on the obligation (IRC § 36(f)(4)(A)–(C))

other_taxes.transition_tax.value: the IRC § 965 transition tax could be paid in eight instalments — 8 percent of the net tax liability for each of the first five, then 15, 20 and 25 percent — with the first due on the unextended due date for the § 965(a) inclusion year and each later one on the following year's unextended due date (IRC § 965(h)(1), (2))

other_taxes.excess_contributions.value: 6 percent of the excess contributions to an individual retirement account, Archer MSA, individual retirement annuity, Coverdell account, health savings account or ABLE account, imposed for each taxable year the excess remains and capped at 6 percent of the account value at the close of the year (IRC § 4973(a))

other_taxes.excess_accumulations.value: 25 percent of the shortfall where less than the required minimum distribution is taken, payable by the payee (IRC § 4974(a))

other_taxes.early_distribution.value: 10 percent of the portion of an early distribution from a qualified retirement plan that is includible in gross income, subject to the exceptions in IRC § 72(t)(2)

other_taxes.shared_responsibility.value: zero — IRC § 5000A(c)(3) still sets out the flat dollar amount and § 5000A(c)(2)(B) the percentage of income, but the percentage is zero for taxable years beginning after 2018 and the flat amount is zero, so the section remains in the Code imposing nothing

injured.definition.value: a spouse on a jointly filed return whose share of the joint overpayment has been applied to a past-due obligation of the other spouse — Form 8379 recovers that share
injured.definition.source: About Form 8379, Injured Spouse Allocation, read at irs.gov/forms-pubs/about-form-8379

injured.offsets.value: past-due child support under IRC § 6402(c), a past-due legally enforceable debt owed to a federal agency under § 6402(d), a past-due state income tax obligation under § 6402(e), and a covered state unemployment compensation debt under § 6402(f) — offsets are run by the Bureau of the Fiscal Service under the Treasury Offset Program, not by the IRS
injured.offsets.source: IRC § 6402(c)–(f) read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/6402 and IRS Topic no. 203 read at irs.gov/taxtopics/tc203

injured.internal_offset.value: an overpayment may first be credited against the couple's own federal tax liability for another year under IRC § 6402(a) — that is an internal credit rather than a Treasury Offset Program offset, and injured spouse relief does not reach a joint liability of both spouses

injured.notice.value: the Bureau of the Fiscal Service, not the IRS, sends the notice showing the original refund, the offset and the agency paid, and the IRS is not told the details — a taxpayer should contact the Bureau unless the refund figure on the notice differs from the return
injured.notice.source: IRS Topic no. 203 (page last reviewed 1 June 2026), read at irs.gov/taxtopics/tc203

innocent.three_routes.value: IRC § 6015(b) understatement relief for a joint filer who did not know and had no reason to know; § 6015(c) separate allocation for a taxpayer divorced, legally separated or living apart for twelve months; and § 6015(f) equitable relief where neither of the others is available

innocent.b_conditions.value: a joint return, an understatement attributable to erroneous items of the other spouse, no knowledge and no reason to know of it, inequity in holding the electing spouse liable on all the facts and circumstances, and an election within two years of the start of collection activity (IRC § 6015(b)(1)(A)–(E))

innocent.c_conditions.value: available only where the electing spouse is no longer married to, or is legally separated from, the other, or was not a member of the same household at any time in the twelve months ending on the date of election — and the election is invalid where the Secretary shows assets were transferred as part of a fraudulent scheme (IRC § 6015(c)(3)(A))

innocent.timing.value: relief under § 6015(b) or (c) must be elected within two years of the start of collection activity; equitable relief under § 6015(f) may be requested for an unpaid liability at any time before the § 6502 collection period expires, and for a paid one within the period for a timely refund claim (IRC § 6015(b)(1)(E), (c)(3)(B), (f)(2))

innocent.tax_court.value: the Tax Court has jurisdiction on a petition filed after the earlier of the final determination notice or six months from the request, and not later than 90 days after the determination notice (IRC § 6015(e)(1)(A))

innocent.refunds.value: a refund is available for relief under § 6015(b) or (f) subject to §§ 6511, 6512(b), 7121 and 7122 — but § 6015(g)(3) allows no credit or refund at all for relief under § 6015(c), which only limits liability

reporting.6041_threshold.value: $2,000 for payments made after 31 December 2025, raised from $600 by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70433(a) and indexed from calendar year 2026 under the new IRC § 6041(h), with the increase rounded to the nearest $100
reporting.6041_threshold.source: IRC § 6041(a), (h) as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70433, read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/6041

reporting.1099k_threshold.value: more than $20,000 **and** more than 200 transactions — both must be exceeded. Pub. L. 119-21 § 70432(a)(1) restored the conjunctive test to IRC § 6050W(e), and § 70432(a)(2) made it effective as if included in the American Rescue Plan provision that had reduced it, so the $600 threshold never operated
reporting.1099k_threshold.source: IRC § 6050W(e) as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70432, read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/6050W

reporting.cash_8300.value: more than $10,000 in cash received in one transaction or two or more related transactions by a person engaged in a trade or business — reported on Form 8300 (IRC § 6050I(a))

reporting.barter.value: a barter exchange is an organization of members providing property or services who jointly contract to trade or barter, and it is a broker required to report its members' exchanges (IRC § 6045(c)(1)(B), (c)(3))

reporting.barter_income.value: the fair market value of property or services received in barter is gross income under IRC § 61(a) whether or not any information return is filed — reporting and taxability are independent questions

reporting.6721_penalty.value: for a return required to be filed in 2027, $340 per return with a calendar year maximum of $4,191,500, reduced to $60 and $698,500 if corrected within 30 days and $130 and $2,095,500 if corrected by 1 August — with lower maxima for a filer whose average annual gross receipts for the three most recent taxable years are $5,000,000 or less

reporting.6721_intentional.value: for intentional disregard, the greater of $690 or 10 percent of the aggregate amount required to be reported correctly, with no calendar year limit (IRC § 6721(e)(2)(A), as adjusted for returns required to be filed in 2027)

reporting.6041_history.value: the $600 figure in IRC § 6041(a) stood unchanged from 1954 until Pub. L. 119-21 § 70433 raised it to $2,000 for payments made after 31 December 2025 — the first time the threshold has ever been indexed
reporting.6041_history.source: IRC § 6041 amendment notes, read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/6041

reporting.1099k_history.value: the reduced threshold enacted by the American Rescue Plan was a single dollar figure of $600 with no transaction count; Pub. L. 119-21 § 70432(a)(2) made its repeal effective as if included in that Act, so it never operated as law for any year
reporting.1099k_history.source: IRC § 6050W(e) amendment and effective date notes, read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/6050W

propsale.rate_breakpoints.value: for 2026 the zero rate on adjusted net capital gain runs to taxable income of $98,900 joint, $66,200 head of household, $49,450 single or married filing separately and $3,300 for an estate or trust; the 15 percent rate runs to $613,700, $579,600, $545,500, $306,850 and $16,250 respectively, with 20 percent above

propsale.collectibles_rate.value: 28 percent on net collectibles gain — the gain on works of art, rugs, antiques, metals, gems, stamps, coins and alcoholic beverages held more than one year (IRC § 1(h)(4), (5))

propsale.unrecaptured_1250.value: 25 percent on unrecaptured section 1250 gain — the depreciation previously taken on real property, to the extent not already recaptured as ordinary income (IRC § 1(h)(1)(E), (6))

propsale.personal_property.value: all property other than real property — real property is land and whatever is permanently affixed to it, so a copyright, a vehicle and a collectible are personal property while land is not
propsale.personal_property.source: IRC § 1221 and the real/personal distinction as used throughout subtitle A, read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/1221

edplan.529_k12_limit.value: $20,000 per beneficiary per year for elementary and secondary expenses, for taxable years beginning after 31 December 2025 — doubled from $10,000 by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70413(b)
edplan.529_k12_limit.source: IRC § 529 as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 §§ 70413, 70414, read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/529

edplan.529_k12_expenses.value: no longer tuition alone: for distributions made after 4 July 2025, curriculum and curricular materials, books and instructional materials, online educational materials, tuition for outside tutoring by an unrelated licensed teacher or subject matter expert, fees for standardised and advanced placement tests and college admission examinations, dual enrolment fees, and educational therapies for students with disabilities (IRC § 529(c)(7))
edplan.529_k12_expenses.source: IRC § 529 as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 §§ 70413, 70414, read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/529

edplan.529_credentialing.value: qualified postsecondary credentialing expenses are now qualified higher education expenses — tuition, fees, books, supplies and equipment for a recognised postsecondary credential program, testing fees required to obtain or maintain the credential, and continuing education fees required to maintain it (IRC § 529(e)(3)(C), (f))
edplan.529_credentialing.source: IRC § 529 as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 §§ 70413, 70414, read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/529

edplan.529_able_rollover.value: permanent — Pub. L. 119-21 § 70117(a) struck the 1 January 2026 end date from the rollover of a § 529 balance to an ABLE account, for taxable years beginning after 31 December 2025
edplan.529_able_rollover.source: IRC § 529 as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 §§ 70413, 70414, read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/529

edplan.coverdell_limit.value: $2,000 of aggregate contributions per beneficiary per year, in cash, and no contribution after the beneficiary attains age 18 (IRC § 530(b)(1)(A)(i)–(iii))

edplan.employer_assistance.value: $5,250 a year excluded from an employee's gross income, made permanent for employer payments of student loan principal or interest by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70412(a) and indexed for the first time from 2027 under the new IRC § 127(d)
edplan.employer_assistance.source: IRC § 127(a)(2), (c)(1)(B), (d) as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70412, read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/127

edplan.student_loan_interest.value: a maximum deduction of $2,500, phasing out for 2026 over modified adjusted gross income of $85,000 to $100,000, or $175,000 to $205,000 on a joint return (IRC § 221(b))
edplan.student_loan_interest.source: IRC § 221(b) read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/221 and Rev. Proc. 2025-32 § 3.29 read at irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/rp-25-32.pdf

estate.basic_exclusion.value: $15,000,000 for a decedent dying in calendar year 2026 — the IRC § 2010(c)(3)(A) basic exclusion amount as raised by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70106, indexed from calendar year 2026 and rounded to the nearest $10,000 under § 2010(c)(3)(B)
estate.basic_exclusion.source: IRC § 2010(c)(3) read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/2010 and Rev. Proc. 2025-32 § 2.14 read at irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/rp-25-32.pdf

estate.gst_exemption.value: $15,000,000 for calendar year 2026 — the IRC § 2631(c) generation-skipping transfer exemption tracks the basic exclusion amount

estate.annual_exclusion.value: $19,000 per donee for calendar year 2026, for gifts other than gifts of future interests (IRC § 2503(b))

estate.noncitizen_spouse.value: $194,000 for calendar year 2026 in place of the ordinary annual exclusion, for gifts to a spouse who is not a United States citizen (IRC §§ 2503 and 2523(i)(2))

estate.portability.value: a surviving spouse may add the deceased spousal unused exclusion amount to their own, but only if the first estate filed a timely and complete estate tax return making the election (IRC § 2010(c)(2)(B), (c)(4), (c)(5)(A))

estate.basis_contrast.value: property acquired from a decedent takes a fair market value basis at death under IRC § 1014(a); property acquired by gift takes the donor's basis under § 1015(a), with a special rule using fair market value where that is lower and the sale produces a loss
estate.basis_contrast.source: IRC §§ 1014(a) and 1015(a), read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/1014 and /1015

estate.life_insurance.value: proceeds payable by reason of death are excluded from gross income under IRC § 101(a)(1), but are in the gross estate under § 2042 where the decedent held any incident of ownership or the proceeds are payable to the estate
estate.life_insurance.source: IRC §§ 101(a) and 2042, read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/101 and /2042

retplan.rmd_age.value: 73 for an individual who attains age 72 after 31 December 2022 and age 73 before 1 January 2033, and 75 for one who attains age 74 after 31 December 2032 — the required beginning date is 1 April of the year following the later of reaching the applicable age or retiring, except that the retirement limb never applies to a 5-percent owner or to an IRA (IRC § 401(a)(9)(C))

retplan.qcd_limit.value: $111,000 of qualified charitable distributions excluded from gross income for 2026, and $55,000 for a one-time distribution to a split-interest entity under IRC § 408(d)(8)(F)(i)(II)
retplan.qcd_limit.source: Notice 2025-67, 2026 amounts relating to retirement plans and IRAs, read at irs.gov

retplan.qcd_conditions.value: paid directly by the trustee to an organization described in IRC § 170(b)(1)(A), other than a supporting organization or a donor advised fund, on or after the date the individual attains age 70½, and only to the extent the distribution would otherwise be includible in gross income (IRC § 408(d)(8)(B))

retplan.qcd_offset.value: the excludable amount is reduced by the excess of deductible IRA contributions made for all taxable years ending on or after the individual attained age 70½ over the reductions already applied — so continuing to deduct IRA contributions after 70½ erodes the exclusion (IRC § 408(d)(8)(A))

retplan.ira_deduction_phaseout.value: for 2026, an active participant's traditional IRA deduction phases out over adjusted gross income of $81,000 to $91,000 for a single filer or head of household and $129,000 to $149,000 on a joint return; where only the spouse is an active participant the range is $242,000 to $252,000; and for a married individual filing separately the applicable amount is zero and is never indexed
retplan.ira_deduction_phaseout.source: Notice 2025-67, 2026 amounts relating to retirement plans and IRAs, read at irs.gov

retplan.catch_up.value: $1,100 for 2026 for an individual who has attained age 50 before the close of the taxable year, under IRC § 219(b)(5)(B)(ii)
retplan.catch_up.source: Notice 2025-67, 2026 amounts relating to retirement plans and IRAs, read at irs.gov

retplan.spousal_rollover.value: only a surviving spouse may treat an inherited individual retirement account as their own or roll it into their own account — any other beneficiary cannot, and must take the balance under the applicable distribution rules instead
retplan.spousal_rollover.source: IRC § 408(d)(3)(C) and § 401(a)(9)(B), read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/408 and /401

retplan.qcd_statutory_base.value: the figure printed in IRC § 408(d)(8)(A) is $100,000, an unindexed statutory base that has not been the operative amount since indexing began — the current limit comes from the annual retirement notice, not from the section
retplan.qcd_statutory_base.source: IRC § 408(d)(8)(A) read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/408, with the 2026 amount in Notice 2025-67 read at irs.gov

divorce.alimony_repeal.value: alimony is neither deductible by the payer nor income to the recipient for any instrument executed after 31 December 2018 — Pub. L. 115-97 § 11051 repealed IRC §§ 71 and 215 outright, and an instrument executed before that date keeps the old treatment unless it is modified and the modification expressly adopts the repeal
divorce.alimony_repeal.source: IRC §§ 71 and 215 as repealed by Pub. L. 115-97 § 11051, read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/71 and /215

divorce.property_transfer.value: no gain or loss is recognised on a transfer of property to a spouse, or to a former spouse where the transfer is incident to the divorce, the transferee takes it as a gift with the transferor's adjusted basis (IRC § 1041(a), (b))

divorce.incident_test.value: a transfer is incident to the divorce if it occurs within one year after the marriage ceases, or is related to the cessation of the marriage (IRC § 1041(c)(1), (2))

divorce.marital_status.value: determined as of the close of the taxable year, except that where a spouse dies during the year it is determined at the date of death; and an individual legally separated under a decree of divorce or separate maintenance is not married (IRC § 7703(a)(1), (2))

divorce.social_security_base.value: $25,000 generally, $32,000 on a joint return, and **zero** for a taxpayer who is married at the close of the year, does not file jointly, and does not live apart from their spouse at all times during the year (IRC § 86(c)(1))

divorce.dependency.value: where the parents are divorced, legally separated, separated under a written agreement, or living apart for the last six months, and the child is in the custody of one or both for more than half the year, the child may be treated as the noncustodial parent's on a release by the custodial parent (IRC § 152(e)(1), (2))

carryover.capital_loss.value: a non-corporate taxpayer deducts capital losses against capital gains plus the lower of $3,000 — $1,500 for a married individual filing separately — or the excess of losses over gains, and the unused balance carries forward indefinitely keeping its short-term or long-term character (IRC §§ 1211(b), 1212(b)(1))
carryover.capital_loss.source: IRC §§ 1211(b) and 1212(b), read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/1211 and /1212

carryover.charitable.value: five succeeding taxable years, in order of time, for contributions exceeding the percentage limitation for the year (IRC § 170(d)(1)(A))

carryover.negative_qbi.value: a negative net amount of qualified business income for a year is treated as a loss from a qualified trade or business in the succeeding taxable year, so it reduces the following year's deduction rather than being lost (IRC § 199A(c)(2))

carryover.minimum_tax_credit.value: indefinite, with no expiry, but usable in any year only up to regular tax liability reduced by other nonrefundable credits less the tentative minimum tax — and generated only by deferral items (IRC § 53(b), (c), (d)(1)(B))

estplan.withholding_ratable.value: tax withheld is deemed paid in equal parts on each of the four installment due dates, whatever the calendar shows, unless the taxpayer establishes the actual withholding dates — and the election may be made separately for wage withholding and for other withholding (IRC § 6654(g))

estplan.annualization_percentages.value: 22.5 percent for the first installment, 45 percent for the second, 67.5 percent for the third and 90 percent for the fourth, applied to the tax on income annualised through the months ending before the installment's due date (IRC § 6654(d)(2)(B), (C)(ii))

estplan.annualization_recapture.value: any reduction obtained by annualising is added back to the next required installment, and to later installments until it has been recaptured in full (IRC § 6654(d)(2)(A)(ii))

estplan.january_filing_rule.value: filing the return and paying the balance in full on or before 31 January of the following year removes the addition to tax for the fourth installment only — the first three stand (IRC § 6654(h))

estplan.farmer_fisherman.value: one installment instead of four, due 15 January of the following year, computed by substituting 66⅔ percent for 90 percent and ignoring the 110 percent rule, with the filing date that cancels it moved to 1 March (IRC § 6654(i))

estplan.farmer_definition.value: gross income from farming or fishing is at least 66⅔ percent of gross income from all sources, tested on either the current year or the preceding year's return (IRC § 6654(i)(2))

estplan.disaster_waiver.value: the Secretary may waive the addition to the extent that, by reason of casualty, disaster or other unusual circumstances, imposing it would be against equity and good conscience (IRC § 6654(e)(3)(A))

estplan.overpayment_credit.value: an overpayment of the preceding year's income tax may be credited against the current year's estimated tax under regulations prescribed by the Secretary (IRC § 6402(b))

timing.cash_receipt.value: an item of gross income is included in the year received, unless the taxpayer's method of accounting properly accounts for it in a different period (IRC § 451(a))

timing.constructive_receipt.value: income is received when credited to the taxpayer's account, set apart, or otherwise made available to be drawn on — but not where control of its receipt is subject to substantial limitations or restrictions (Reg. § 1.451-2(a))

timing.cash_payment.value: deductions are taken in the year paid, except that an expenditure creating an asset whose useful life extends substantially beyond the close of the year may not be deductible, or deductible only in part, that year (Reg. § 1.461-1(a)(1))

timing.prepaid_interest.value: interest a cash-method taxpayer pays that is allocable to a period after the close of the year is charged to capital account and treated as paid in the period to which it is allocable — so prepaying a January mortgage payment in December buys nothing (IRC § 461(g)(1))

timing.points_exception.value: points on debt incurred to purchase or improve, and secured by, the taxpayer's principal residence escape the prepaid interest rule to the extent paying them is an established business practice in the area and the amount does not exceed what is generally charged there (IRC § 461(g)(2))

timing.charitable_delivery.value: a contribution is made when delivery is effected — an unconditionally delivered or mailed check that later clears counts on the date of delivery or mailing, and a properly endorsed stock certificate on the date of delivery or mailing, but a certificate handed to the donor's own bank or broker for transfer counts only when the stock is transferred on the corporation's books (Reg. § 1.170A-1(b))

timing.itemize_election.value: no itemized deduction is allowed at all unless the individual elects to itemize on the return, and the election may be changed under regulations (IRC § 63(e))

timing.ira_deemed_made.value: a contribution made by the unextended due date of the return is deemed made on the last day of the preceding taxable year if it is made on account of that year — extensions do not count (IRC § 219(f)(3))

timing.nonrefundable_ceiling.value: the subpart A nonrefundable credits may not exceed regular tax liability reduced by the foreign tax credit, plus the tax imposed by IRC § 55(a) — so a year with too little tax wastes them (IRC § 26(a))

timing.wash_sale_window.value: 61 days — beginning 30 days before the sale and ending 30 days after it; acquiring substantially identical stock or securities, or a contract or option to acquire them, inside that window disallows the loss (IRC § 1091(a))

timing.related_party_matching.value: a deduction for an expense or interest owed to a related person on the cash method is deferred until the day the amount is includible in that person's gross income (IRC § 267(a)(2))

salt.superseded_flat_cap.value: $10,000, or $5,000 for a married individual filing separately — the flat figure that stood in IRC § 164(b)(6)(B) for taxable years 2018 through 2024 until Pub. L. 119-21 § 70120(a)(2) replaced it with the applicable limitation amount
salt.superseded_flat_cap.source: IRC § 164, including the amendment note to § 164(b)(6)(B), read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/164

character.ordinary_income_defined.value: any gain from the sale or exchange of property that is neither a capital asset nor IRC § 1231(b) property, together with any gain another provision treats as ordinary income (IRC § 64)

character.ordinary_loss_defined.value: any loss from the sale or exchange of property that is not a capital asset, together with any loss another provision treats as ordinary loss (IRC § 65)

sec1231.trade_or_business_property.value: depreciable property used in the trade or business and held for more than 1 year, and real property used in the trade or business and held for more than 1 year — excluding inventory, property held primarily for sale to customers, self-created intangibles in the creator's hands and certain government publications (IRC § 1231(b)(1))

sec1231.lookback.value: net section 1231 gain is ordinary income to the extent of non-recaptured net section 1231 losses — the net section 1231 losses of the 5 most recent preceding taxable years, reduced by any already recaptured (IRC § 1231(c))

qsbs.exclusion_tiers.value: for stock acquired after 4 July 2025, 50 percent of the gain at 3 years held, 75 percent at 4 years and 100 percent at 5 years or more; stock acquired on or before that date keeps the older regime, which requires more than 5 years (IRC § 1202(a)(1), (5), (6))
qsbs.exclusion_tiers.source: IRC § 1202, including the note giving the enactment date of Pub. L. 119-21 as 4 July 2025, read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/1202

qsbs.per_issuer_limit.value: the greater of the applicable dollar limit or 10 times the aggregate adjusted bases of the stock disposed of that year — the dollar limit being $15,000,000 for stock acquired after 4 July 2025, indexed for taxable years beginning after 2026, and $10,000,000 for stock acquired on or before it, halved on a separate return (IRC § 1202(b))

qsbs.gross_assets.value: $75,000,000 of aggregate gross assets — cash plus the aggregate adjusted bases of other property — at all times before the issuance and immediately after it (IRC § 1202(d)(1), (2))

qsbs.superseded_regime.value: a cliff at a holding period of more than 5 years with no exclusion below it, a $10,000,000 per-issuer dollar limit and a $50,000,000 aggregate gross assets test — the rules that governed before Pub. L. 119-21 § 70431 and that still govern stock acquired on or before 4 July 2025
qsbs.superseded_regime.source: IRC § 1202 and its 2025 amendment notes, read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/1202

status.joint_and_several.value: where a joint return is made the tax is computed on aggregate income and the liability for it is joint and several — each spouse is liable for the whole of it, without regard to who earned the income or made the error (IRC § 6013(d)(3))

status.separate_to_joint.value: a couple who filed separate returns may still make a joint return for that year, but not after 3 years from the unextended due date, nor after a notice of deficiency has been mailed and the spouse has petitioned the Tax Court, nor after either spouse has sued for recovery of any part of the tax, nor after a closing agreement or a compromise (IRC § 6013(b))

status.joint_to_separate.value: there is no corresponding provision — IRC § 6013(b) runs one way only, so once a joint return is filed the couple may not switch to separate returns for that year after the due date has passed
status.joint_to_separate.source: IRC § 6013, read in full at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/6013

status.considered_unmarried.value: a married individual who files separately, maintains a household that is for more than half the year the principal place of abode of a child for whom a dependency deduction is allowable, furnishes over half the cost of maintaining it, and whose spouse is not a member of the household during the last 6 months of the year, is not considered married (IRC § 7703(b))

status.hoh_gateway.value: head of household requires the individual to be not married at the close of the year and not a surviving spouse — a married individual reaches it only through the IRC § 7703(b) route, which IRC § 2(c) imports for this purpose (IRC § 2(b)(1), (c))

status.mfs_standard_deduction.value: zero where either spouse itemizes — the standard deduction is denied to a married individual filing separately if the other spouse itemizes, so the choice binds both (IRC § 63(c)(6)(A))

status.mfs_denied.value: the dependent care credit (IRC § 21(e)(2)), the education credits (§ 25A(g)(6)), the earned income credit (§ 32(d)(1)) and the student loan interest deduction (§ 221(e)(2)) are each allowed to a married individual only on a joint return
status.mfs_denied.source: IRC §§ 21, 25A, 32 and 221, each read at law.cornell.edu

status.mfs_social_security_base.value: zero — a taxpayer married at the close of the year who does not file jointly and does not live apart from the spouse at all times during the year has a base amount and an adjusted base amount of zero, so benefits are taxable from the first dollar (IRC § 86(c)(1)(C), (2)(C))

status.mfs_rental_allowance.value: halved to $12,500 with the phase-out range halved to $50,000 and $100,000 for a married individual filing separately who lives apart from the spouse at all times during the year — and denied entirely to one who does not (IRC § 469(i)(5))

status.mfs_ira_phaseout.value: spouses who file separately and live apart at all times during the year are each treated as not married for the IRC § 219(g) active participant phase-out — those who live together are not, and the phase-out range for them is unindexed and very low (IRC § 219(g)(4))

refundclaim.general_period.value: the later of 3 years from the time the return was filed or 2 years from the time the tax was paid — and 2 years from payment only, where no return was filed (IRC § 6511(a))

refundclaim.early_return.value: a return filed before the last day prescribed for filing it is treated as filed on that last day, and tax paid before the last day prescribed for payment is treated as paid on that day — both determined without regard to extensions (IRC § 6513(a))

refundclaim.withholding_deemed_paid.value: tax withheld at source during a calendar year is deemed paid on the 15th day of the fourth month following the close of the taxable year, and estimated tax on the unextended due date of the return — which is what makes the 2-year branch of IRC § 6511(a) run from the same date for most individuals (IRC § 6513(b))

refundclaim.lookback_cap.value: a claim filed inside the 3-year period recovers only tax paid in the 3 years plus any extension period immediately preceding the claim; a claim filed outside it recovers only tax paid in the 2 years immediately preceding (IRC § 6511(b)(2))

refundclaim.bad_debt_period.value: 7 years from the date prescribed for filing the return for the year concerned, where the claim relates to a debt that became worthless under IRC § 166 or § 832(c) or a worthless security under § 165(g), or to the effect of such a deduction on a carryover (IRC § 6511(d)(1))

refundclaim.carryback_period.value: 3 years after the time prescribed for filing the return, including extensions, for the year of the net operating loss or net capital loss that produces the carryback — measured from the loss year, not the year being amended (IRC § 6511(d)(2)(A))

refundclaim.foreign_tax_period.value: 10 years from the date prescribed for filing the return for the year in which the foreign taxes were actually paid or accrued (IRC § 6511(d)(3)(A))

refundclaim.financial_disability.value: the periods are suspended while an individual is financially disabled — unable to manage financial affairs by reason of a medically determinable impairment expected to result in death or lasting at least 12 months, proved as the Secretary requires — but not for any period in which a spouse or another person was authorised to act on the individual's behalf in financial matters (IRC § 6511(h))

refundclaim.combat_zone.value: the period of service in the combat zone or contingency operation, plus any period of continuous qualified hospitalization for an injury received there, plus the next 180 days, is disregarded (IRC § 7508(a))

refundclaim.disaster.value: the Secretary may specify a period of up to 1 year to be disregarded for a taxpayer affected by a federally declared disaster, a significant fire, or a terroristic or military action — and the postponement reaches the amount of any credit or refund, not merely the filing act (IRC § 7508A(a))

perjury.declaration_required.value: except as the Secretary otherwise provides, any return, declaration, statement or other document required under the internal revenue laws or regulations must contain, or be verified by, a written declaration that it is made under the penalties of perjury (IRC § 6065)

perjury.signature_required.value: every such document must be signed in accordance with the forms or regulations the Secretary prescribes, and the Secretary must provide procedures accepting electronic signatures (IRC § 6061)

perjury.signature_presumption.value: a name signed to a return, statement or other document is prima facie evidence for all purposes that the document was actually signed by that person (IRC § 6064)

perjury.7206_elements.value: willfully making and subscribing a return, statement or other document verified by a penalties-of-perjury declaration which the signer does not believe to be true and correct as to every material matter — a felony, with no requirement that any tax be owed (IRC § 7206(1))

perjury.7206_sentence.value: up to 3 years' imprisonment, and a fine of up to $250,000 for an individual or $500,000 for an organization — not the $100,000 and $500,000 printed in IRC § 7206, which 18 U.S.C. § 3571(b)(3) and (c)(3) supersede because § 7206 contains no specific reference exempting it under § 3571(e)
perjury.7206_sentence.source: IRC § 7206 and 18 U.S.C. § 3571, both read at law.cornell.edu

perjury.7207_offence.value: willfully delivering or disclosing to the Secretary any list, return, account, statement or other document known to be fraudulent or false as to any material matter — a misdemeanor carrying up to 1 year's imprisonment (IRC § 7207)

perjury.7201_sentence.value: up to 5 years' imprisonment for willfully attempting in any manner to evade or defeat any tax or its payment, with the fine again set by 18 U.S.C. § 3571 rather than by the $100,000 printed in the section (IRC § 7201)
perjury.7201_sentence.source: IRC § 7201 and 18 U.S.C. § 3571, both read at law.cornell.edu

perjury.civil_fraud.value: 75 percent of the portion of an underpayment attributable to fraud — and once the Secretary establishes that any portion is fraudulent, the whole underpayment is treated as fraudulent except as to any portion the taxpayer establishes is not (IRC § 6663)

estate.gross_estate_definition.value: the value at the time of death of all property, real or personal, tangible or intangible, wherever situated, to the extent of the decedent's interest in it (IRC §§ 2031(a), 2033)
estate.gross_estate_definition.source: IRC §§ 2031 and 2033, read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/2031 and /2033

estate.taxable_estate_definition.value: the gross estate less the deductions allowed by part IV — funeral and administration expenses, claims against the estate and unpaid mortgages under IRC § 2053, losses under § 2054, charitable transfers under § 2055 and the marital deduction under § 2056 (IRC §§ 2051, 2053(a))
estate.taxable_estate_definition.source: IRC §§ 2051 and 2053, read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/2051 and /2053

estate.tax_computation.value: a tentative tax on the sum of the taxable estate and adjusted taxable gifts, reduced by the gift tax that would have been payable on post-1976 gifts under current rates — so lifetime gifts enlarge the base rather than reducing the exclusion arithmetic (IRC § 2001(b))

estate.top_rate.value: 40 percent of the excess over $1,000,000, on top of $345,800 — the top bracket of the IRC § 2001(c) unified rate schedule, which every estate large enough to owe tax is entirely inside

estate.applicable_credit.value: the tentative tax that IRC § 2001(c) would produce on the applicable exclusion amount — a credit against tax, not a deduction from the estate, and the reason the exclusion is worth exactly the tax on it and no more (IRC § 2010(c)(1))

estate.applicable_exclusion.value: the basic exclusion amount plus, for a surviving spouse, the deceased spousal unused exclusion amount (IRC § 2010(c)(2))

estate.alternate_valuation.value: an irrevocable election to value everything six months after death, or at the date of disposition for property disposed of within those six months — available only if it decreases both the gross estate and the sum of the estate and generation-skipping taxes after credits (IRC § 2032(a), (c), (d))

estate.three_year_rule.value: property transferred, or a power relinquished, within the 3-year period ending at death is pulled back into the gross estate where it would have been included under IRC § 2036, 2037, 2038 or 2042 had the interest or power been retained (IRC § 2035(a))

estate.insurance_inclusion.value: insurance on the decedent's life is in the gross estate to the extent receivable by the executor, and to the extent receivable by anyone else where the decedent possessed any incident of ownership at death, exercisable alone or with another (IRC § 2042)

estate.return_threshold.value: a return is required where the gross estate of a citizen or resident exceeds the basic exclusion amount in effect for the calendar year of death — $60,000 of United States situs property for a nonresident who is not a citizen (IRC § 6018(a))

estate.return_due_date.value: 9 months after the date of death (IRC § 6075(a))

estate.closely_held_deferral.value: where an interest in a closely held business exceeds 35 percent of the adjusted gross estate, the executor may elect to pay the attributable share of the tax in up to 10 equal installments (IRC § 6166(a))

estate.superseded_exclusion.value: $5,000,000 indexed, doubled to $10,000,000 indexed for decedents dying after 2017 and before 2026 by a temporary subparagraph that was to lapse — Pub. L. 119-21 § 70106(a) substituted $15,000,000 for $5,000,000, struck the temporary subparagraph and re-based the indexing on calendar year 2025
estate.superseded_exclusion.source: IRC § 2010(c)(3) and its 2017 and 2025 amendment notes, read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/2010

joint.consideration_rule.value: the whole value of jointly held property with right of survivorship is in the decedent's gross estate, except the part shown to have originally belonged to the other owner and never to have been acquired from the decedent for less than adequate and full consideration (IRC § 2040(a))

joint.proportionate_exception.value: where the survivor did furnish consideration, the excluded part is the proportion of the whole value that the survivor's consideration bears to the total cost of acquisition and capital additions — and only consideration not itself traceable to the decedent counts (IRC § 2040(a); Reg. § 20.2040-1(a)(2))
joint.proportionate_exception.source: IRC § 2040 and 26 CFR § 20.2040-1, read at law.cornell.edu

joint.inherited_interest.value: where the joint interest was itself acquired by gift, devise, bequest or inheritance, the decedent's fractional share is included and the consideration test never runs (IRC § 2040(a) second proviso; Reg. § 20.2040-1(a)(1))
joint.inherited_interest.source: IRC § 2040 and 26 CFR § 20.2040-1, read at law.cornell.edu

joint.qualified_joint_interest.value: exactly one-half, whatever either spouse contributed — for property held by the decedent and the decedent's spouse as tenants by the entirety, or as joint tenants with right of survivorship where the two spouses are the only joint tenants (IRC § 2040(b))

joint.noncitizen_spouse.value: IRC § 2040(b) does not apply where the surviving spouse is not a United States citizen, so the consideration-furnished test of § 2040(a) governs instead and the marital deduction is denied unless the property passes in a qualified domestic trust (IRC § 2056(d)(1))

joint.tenancy_in_common.value: a tenancy in common has no survivorship, so IRC § 2040 never applies to it — the decedent's undivided fractional interest is in the gross estate under § 2033 and passes by will or intestacy rather than to the co-tenant
joint.tenancy_in_common.source: IRC §§ 2033 and 2040, read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/2033 and /2040

joint.basis_follows_inclusion.value: basis under IRC § 1014 follows inclusion — property required to be included in the gross estate by reason of death, form of ownership or other conditions takes a date-of-death value basis, so a survivor who excluded half from the estate steps up only that half (IRC § 1014(b)(9))

joint.community_property_basis.value: the surviving spouse's own one-half of community property takes a date-of-death basis too, provided at least half of the whole community interest was includible in the decedent's gross estate — a full step-up on both halves, which no form of joint tenancy achieves (IRC § 1014(b)(6))

marital.deduction.value: unlimited — the value of any interest in property passing from the decedent to the surviving spouse is deducted in full, but only to the extent that interest is included in determining the value of the gross estate (IRC § 2056(a))

marital.terminable_interest.value: no deduction for an interest that will terminate or fail on the lapse of time or on an event, where an interest in the same property passed from the decedent for less than adequate consideration to someone other than the spouse and that person may enjoy the property after the spouse's interest ends (IRC § 2056(b)(1))

marital.life_estate_power.value: a life estate qualifies where the spouse is entitled for life to all the income, payable at least annually, with a power in the spouse alone to appoint the entire interest to the spouse or the spouse's estate, and no power in anyone else to appoint any part of it to anyone else (IRC § 2056(b)(5))

marital.qtip.value: qualified terminable interest property is treated as passing to the spouse — property passing from the decedent in which the spouse has a qualifying income interest for life and to which the executor's election applies, the spouse being entitled to all the income payable at least annually (IRC § 2056(b)(7))

marital.qdot.value: a trust requiring at least one United States citizen or domestic corporation trustee, providing that no non-income distribution may be made unless that trustee can withhold the tax on it, meeting the Secretary's collection requirements, and covered by the executor's election (IRC § 2056A(a))

marital.gift_deduction.value: an unlimited deduction in computing taxable gifts for the value of an interest transferred by gift to a donee who is the donor's spouse at the time of the gift, subject to a terminable interest rule of its own (IRC § 2523(a), (b))

portability.dsue_definition.value: the lesser of the basic exclusion amount, or the applicable exclusion amount of the last deceased spouse reduced by the amount on which the tentative tax was determined under IRC § 2001(b)(1) on that spouse's estate (IRC § 2010(c)(4))

portability.election.value: made by the executor of the estate of the deceased spouse, on an estate tax return for that estate on which the amount is computed, filed within the time prescribed including extensions — and once made it is irrevocable (IRC § 2010(c)(5)(A))

portability.last_spouse_rule.value: only the last deceased spouse's unused exclusion is available — a survivor who remarries and outlives a second spouse loses any unused amount from the first, and amounts from successive spouses are not stacked (IRC § 2010(c)(4)(B)(i))

portability.reopened_examination.value: notwithstanding IRC § 6501, the Secretary may examine the deceased spouse's return to determine the unused exclusion amount after the ordinary assessment period for that estate has closed (IRC § 2010(c)(5)(B))

deathben.insurance_income_exclusion.value: proceeds under a life insurance contract paid by reason of the death of the insured are excluded from gross income, subject to the transfer for value rule and the other exceptions in IRC § 101(a)(2), (d), (f) and (j)

deathben.annuity_inclusion.value: the gross estate includes an annuity or other payment receivable by a beneficiary by reason of surviving the decedent under any contract other than life insurance, where an annuity or payment was payable to the decedent, or the decedent had the right to receive one, for life or for a period not ascertainable without reference to death or not in fact ending before death (IRC § 2039(a))

deathben.ird_definition.value: items of gross income of a decedent not properly includible in the period ending with death are taxed to whoever receives them — the estate, the person acquiring the right by reason of the death, or a person receiving it by bequest, devise or inheritance from the decedent (IRC § 691(a)(1))

deathben.ird_estate_tax_deduction.value: a deduction for the estate tax attributable to the item, in the same ratio that the item's estate tax value bears to the estate tax value of all such items — so the same dollars are not taxed twice without relief (IRC § 691(c)(1))

deathben.no_step_up.value: income in respect of a decedent takes no fair market value basis — IRC § 1014(c) excepts it from the general rule, so a traditional IRA passes to a beneficiary with its income tax charge intact

deathben.ten_year_rule.value: 10 years — for a defined contribution plan, the whole interest must be distributed within 10 years of the employee's death, whether or not distributions had begun, except for an eligible designated beneficiary (IRC § 401(a)(9)(H)(i))

deathben.eligible_designated_beneficiary.value: five categories, tested as of the date of the employee's death — the surviving spouse, a child of the employee who has not reached majority, a disabled individual within IRC § 72(m)(7), a chronically ill individual within § 7702B(c)(2) with a certification of indefinite and lengthy inability, and any individual not more than 10 years younger than the employee (IRC § 401(a)(9)(E)(ii))

deathben.minor_child_transition.value: a minor child ceases to be an eligible designated beneficiary on reaching majority, and the remainder must then be distributed within 10 years of that date (IRC § 401(a)(9)(E)(iii))

deathben.edb_death.value: when an eligible designated beneficiary dies before the interest is fully distributed, the exception stops — the beneficiary's own beneficiary gets 10 years from that death and nothing longer (IRC § 401(a)(9)(H)(iii))

estatefile.706_threshold_reduced.value: the filing threshold is reduced, but not below zero, by post-1976 adjusted taxable gifts and by any specific exemption allowed under the repealed IRC § 2521 for gifts after 8 September 1976 — so an estate below the basic exclusion amount can still be required to file (IRC § 6018(a)(3))

estatefile.1041_threshold.value: $600 of gross income for the taxable year for a domestic estate; a trust files on any taxable income, or on $600 of gross income whatever the taxable income; and either files where any beneficiary is a nonresident alien, whatever the income (IRC § 6012(a)(3), (4), (5))

estatefile.1041_due_date.value: the 15th day of the fourth month following the close of the taxable year — 15 April for a calendar year estate (IRC § 6072(a))

estatefile.fiscal_year.value: an estate may adopt a fiscal year, and a fiscal year must be a period of 12 months ending on the last day of a month other than December — so an estate's first year can be short but cannot end mid-month (IRC § 441(e))

estatefile.645_election.value: where the executor and the trustee of a qualified revocable trust both elect, the trust is treated and taxed as part of the estate rather than as a separate trust (IRC § 645(a))

estatefile.645_applicable_date.value: 2 years after the date of death where no estate tax return is required, and 6 months after the final determination of the chapter 11 liability where one is (IRC § 645(b)(2))

estatefile.filing_extension.value: the Secretary may grant a reasonable extension of time to file, and outside the case of taxpayers abroad no such extension may exceed 6 months (IRC § 6081(a))

estatefile.payment_extension.value: up to 12 months for estate tax shown on the return under the general rule, and for reasonable cause up to 10 years from the IRC § 6151(a) payment date — with a separate 4-year limit for a deficiency, unavailable where the deficiency is due to negligence, intentional disregard or fraud (IRC § 6161(a)(1), (a)(2), (b)(2), (b)(3))

estatefile.1041_unindexed.value: $600 — the IRC § 6012(a)(3) gross income threshold for an estate, which is not indexed and has stood at that figure since the 1954 Code, so inflation alone has steadily widened the population of estates required to file

giftsplit.general_rule.value: a gift by one spouse to anyone other than the other spouse is treated as made one-half by each, but only where both spouses were citizens or residents at the time of the gift (IRC § 2513(a)(1))

giftsplit.all_or_nothing.value: consent applies to all gifts made by either spouse to third parties during the calendar year — it cannot be given for one gift and withheld for another (IRC § 2513(a)(2))

giftsplit.marital_status.value: the spouses must be married at the time of the gift, and the donor's spouse must not remarry during the remainder of the calendar year (IRC § 2513(a)(1))

giftsplit.general_power_exception.value: splitting is unavailable for a gift of an interest in property in which the donor creates a general power of appointment, within IRC § 2514(c), in the consenting spouse (IRC § 2513(a)(1))

giftsplit.consent_deadline.value: consent may be signified any time after the close of the calendar year but not after 15 April following it — unless neither spouse has filed for that year by then, in which case not after either spouse files — and never after a notice of deficiency for that year has been sent to either spouse (IRC § 2513(b)(2))

giftsplit.revocation.value: a consent signified on or before 15 April may be revoked up to that date and no later; a consent signified after 15 April may not be revoked at all (IRC § 2513(c))

giftsplit.joint_liability.value: consenting makes each spouse jointly and severally liable for the entire gift tax of both for that calendar year (IRC § 2513(d))

giftsplit.return_requirement.value: a return is required of any individual making a transfer by gift other than one excluded by IRC § 2503(b) or (e), one deductible under § 2523, or a qualifying entire-interest charitable transfer under § 2522 — so a split gift that exceeds one annual exclusion but not two still requires a return from the donor (IRC § 6019)

gift.statutory_face_amount.value: $10,000 — the figure IRC § 2503(b)(1) still prints on its face, which has not been the operative annual exclusion since 1998; § 2503(b)(2) does the indexing and the section itself never states the current amount

annualex.per_donee.value: per donee per calendar year, and the exclusion applies to the first gifts made to that person during the year — there is no aggregate cap on the number of donees (IRC § 2503(b)(1))

annualex.future_interest.value: no part of a gift of a future interest may be excluded — a future interest being a reversion, remainder or other interest limited to commence in use, possession or enjoyment at some future date, while an unrestricted right to the immediate use, possession or enjoyment of property or its income is a present interest (Reg. § 25.2503-3(a), (b))

annualex.indexing.value: indexed from the statutory $10,000 by the IRC § 1(f)(3) cost-of-living adjustment substituting calendar year 1997, and rounded down to the next lowest multiple of $1,000 — which is why the figure moves in whole thousands and can stand still for a year (IRC § 2503(b)(2))

annualex.minor_trust.value: a gift to someone under 21 is not a future interest if the property and its income may be expended by or for the donee before 21, and to the extent unexpended will pass to the donee at 21 or, on earlier death, to the donee's estate or as the donee appoints under a general power (IRC § 2503(c))

annualex.qualified_transfer.value: tuition paid directly to an educational organization described in IRC § 170(b)(1)(A)(ii), and amounts paid directly to a provider of medical care within § 213(d), are not transfers by gift at all — unlimited in amount and additional to the annual exclusion (IRC § 2503(e))

annualex.529_election.value: a contribution to a qualified tuition program is a completed present-interest gift to the beneficiary and is expressly not a qualified transfer, but a donor may elect to spread the excess over the annual exclusion ratably across the 5-year period beginning with that year (IRC § 529(c)(2))

annualex.able_account.value: a contribution to an ABLE account established under IRC § 529A is expressly not a future interest, so the annual exclusion is available for it (Reg. § 25.2503-3(a))

annualex.artwork_loan.value: a loan of archaeological, historic or creative tangible personal property to a § 501(c)(3) organization other than a private foundation, for a use related to its exempt purpose, is not a transfer at all (IRC § 2503(g))

annualex.pension_waiver.value: a waiver before the participant's death of a survivor benefit under IRC § 401(a)(11) or § 417 is not treated as a transfer by gift (IRC § 2503(f))

annualex.noncitizen_spouse_mechanism.value: where the donee spouse is not a citizen the marital deduction is denied and IRC § 2503(b) is applied to those gifts by substituting $100,000 for $10,000 — so the larger figure is the ordinary annual exclusion computed from a different base, indexed the same way (IRC § 2523(i))

giftcredit.amount.value: the applicable credit amount that would be in effect under IRC § 2010(c) if the donor died at the end of the calendar year, reduced by the credit allowable for all preceding calendar periods — so it is the same credit as the estate tax credit, drawn on during life (IRC § 2505(a))

giftcredit.recomputation.value: the credit allowed for preceding calendar periods is recomputed at the current year's rates rather than the rates that applied when those gifts were made (IRC § 2505(a), closing sentence)

giftcredit.ceiling.value: the credit for a calendar year may not exceed the gift tax imposed for that year — it cannot create a refund and unused amounts are not paid out, they simply remain available (IRC § 2505(c))

giftcredit.citizenship.value: the credit is allowed to a citizen or resident of the United States; a nonresident who is not a citizen gets no unified credit against gift tax at all, though the annual exclusion still applies (IRC § 2505(a))

gifttax.cumulative_computation.value: a tentative tax at the IRC § 2001(c) rates on the aggregate taxable gifts of this year and all preceding calendar periods, less a tentative tax on the aggregate of the preceding periods alone — so each year's gifts are taxed at the marginal rate the cumulative total has reached (IRC § 2502(a))
